title: Sean McVay on Kyle Shanahan accident: I talked to him, he's got an incredible perspective
summary: Shanahan suffered serious injuries in a car accident and is not able to perform his full coaching duties to start training camp.
full_text: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan is recovering from serious injuries after a car accident on July 14, and his friend and rival Sean McVay was among the first to reach out to him. McVay, the Rams head coach who worked with Shanahan for four years when they were young assistants in Washington, said Shanahan is in good spirits. “Most importantly, thank God he and the other person involved is okay,” McVay said. “Perspective is everything. We talk about that all the time as coaches, and everybody goes through different things. I think the most important thing is that he's on the road to recovery. His wife Mandy, and he's got a beautiful family, and I think any time that something like that happens, it shakes you up a little bit. But most importantly, I have talked to him. My thoughts and prayers are with him and his family, and I know he's got an incredible perspective on it all. And Kyle's a stud. I have as much respect for him as anybody and he's a friend of mine, and I love him and hope that he's going to have a great recovery.” Shanahan reportedly has a severe concussion, multiple broken bones, and lacerations requiring 40 stitches on his face. He will be coaching on a limited basis in training camp. McVay and Shanahan were hired to coach NFC West rivals in 2017. Shanahan's 49ers are 11-7 against McVay's Rams in the regular season. McVay and the Rams won their only playoff meeting, in the NFC Championship Game after the 2021 season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Giants waive linebacker Cam Jones and defensive lineman C.J. Ravenell
summary: The Giants opened up two spots on their 90-player roster ahead of training camp.
full_text: '' The Giants opened up two spots on their 90-player roster ahead of training camp. Linebacker Cam Jones and defensive lineman C.J. Ravenell were both waived. Jones signed with the Giants in March but missed time during offseason workouts with what coach John Harbaugh described as an injury he suffered while moving boxes into his new home. Jones spent last season with the Jets, appearing in 10 games, and had played in all 17 games each of the two previous seasons with the Chiefs. He primarily plays on special teams. Although there's no word on any box-moving injuries, Ravenell was waived with a Non-Football Injury designation. He previously played for Harbaugh on the Ravens in 2024, and spent 2025 on the Titans.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Macdonald on ownership change: "We're entering a new chapter in our organization's history"
summary: The Seahawks opened training camp on Saturday, only two weeks after the organization announced that the team would be sold to a group led by Vinod Khosla, pending league approval.
full_text: '' The Seahawks opened training camp on Saturday, only two weeks after the organization announced that the team would be sold to a group led by Vinod Khosla, pending league approval. Coach Mike Macdonald addressed the looming change in his first press conference of training camp. “We haven't had much interaction yet, and everything is about the same as it's been," Macdonald told reporters. "Nothing's changed on our front, nor will it for the foreseeable future. So that's how we're approaching everything. We had great visits with all the folks that were here. The best way to describe my mentality is that I'm excited to get going. "We're thankful for Jody [Allen] and the things that her and the rest of the ownership group did, especially since I've been here, it’s been fantastic and hopefully the rest of the 12s feel the same way as they should. Now we're entering a new chapter in our organization's history. That’s a cause for excitement as well.” Macdonald said he had a brief meeting with the new owners. "You can always talk on the phone and do Zooms, but being in person is a different experience, which I definitely appreciated,” Macdonald said. With the Khosla group ready to pay a record $9.612 billion for the Seahawks, it will be theirs to run as they see fit. They should see fit to let the organization run at it has. It's clearly not broken; nothing needs to be fixed.
author: Mike Florio

title: Trey McBride regrets offseason comments about Cardinals fans
summary: Cardinals tight end Trey McBride had some things to say about Cardinals fans during the offseason.
full_text: '' Cardinals tight end Trey McBride had some things to say about Cardinals fans during the offseason. He now says he wishes he hadn't said them. "Yeah, I probably shouldn’t have said that ," McBride told reporters on Saturday, via Josh Weinfuss of ESPN. "It came out wrong, and obviously the fanbase is great. We have a tremendous fanbase. Arizona's been here, loyal fans to all the sports teams here, and we're very lucky to have a lot of these guys, and we're going to have a great season. We're going to win games and we're going to make sure those fans have something proud to cheer for. "I love it here in Arizona, and I hope they love me too, but it's a special place. The fans are great, and I'm excited for this year to give them something to be proud of." Here's what he said, in a visit to the Bussin' With The Boys podcast: "Living in Arizona, no one's from Arizona. Everyone has kind of moved in from another state, so they're all fans of their own teams, so now you have the Arizona that sits there and there's no Arizona fans in Arizona. So it's a tough deal. Hopefully, we start winning some games and we can bring some of those fans back." The simple reality is that the Cardinals aren't currently competitive. They've been to the playoffs once since 2016. And they're stuck in a division with three Super Bowl contenders. Winning draws fans. For plenty of franchises, no one wants to show up to watch a team that isn't competitive. McBride has apparently figured it out. And he's one of the bright spots on a roster that needs plenty of work. Until that happens, why should anyone living in Arizona spend hundreds of dollars and waste a day supporting the team?
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike Macdonald noncommittal on S Nick Emmanwori's availability for Week 1
summary: Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori required arthroscopic surgery on his right ankle earlier this month.
full_text: ' Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori required arthroscopic surgery on his right ankle earlier this month. Emmanwori injured the ankle during practice four days before Super Bowl LX. He played 70 of 72 defensive snaps against the Patriots, but the ankle never bounced back in the offseason. "It’s the ankle from the Super Bowl,” coach Mike Macdonald said Saturday, via Gregg Bell of The News Tribune . “I guess the best way to describe it is, it’s something he’s been dealing with since the Super Bowl. He was able to perform, was able to train and do some things in the offseason program. But [he] just got to the point where it was the best for him, really just best for him in the long term, just go get it fixed. So that’s what he all decided to do. “Really, [it’s] the best for him for now and the foreseeable future, the rest of his career.” Macdonald was noncommittal about Emmanwori's return. He was asked multiple times whether he expects Emmanwori to play in the season opener without a definitive answer. “I don’t know,” Macdonald said. “I mean, could he play in the opener? Sure.” Emmanwori is expected back before the start of the season, Bell reports, but Macdonald wants to avoid a timeline so as not to pressure Emmanwori to rush back. Emmanwori is on the active/physically unable to perform list.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike lands on PUP but cleared to return
summary: Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike injured his neck in Week 2 last season and has not seen the field since.
full_text: ' Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike injured his neck in Week 2 last season and has not seen the field since. He will begin training camp on the active/physically unable to perform list, but Madubuike has come a long way after 10 months of uncertainty over whether he would ever return. Jeff Zrebiec of TheAthletic.com reports that independent doctors have cleared Madubuike to return and the two-time Pro Bowler could practice as soon as next week. Ravens General Manager Eric DeCosta had expressed optimism earlier this month, saying "everything looks to be pointed in the right direction" in Madubuike's return. The Ravens also placed nose tackles Travis Jones (pectoral) and John Jenkins (undisclosed), linebacker Teddye Buchanan (knee), outside linebacker Adisa Isaac (elbow) and cornerback Bilhal Kone (knee) on the active/PUP list. Jones, who led the team with five sacks last year, is working his way back from surgery, per Zrebiec. Center Corey Bullock will start camp on the non-football illness list.
author: Charean Williams

title: Despite ongoing legal issue, Alaric Jackson will practice with Rams
summary: Even though Rams tackle Alaric Jackson won't be charged with a felony following an offseason domestic battery accusation, he could be entering a diversion program in lieu of a misdemeanor prosecution.
full_text: ' Even though Rams tackle Alaric Jackson won't be charged with a felony following an offseason domestic battery accusation, he could be entering a diversion program in lieu of a misdemeanor prosecution. Which would likely result in another Personal Conduct Policy suspension. For now, Jackson will participate in Rams training camp. Coach Sean McVay confirmed that Jackson is present, and that he'll "be a part of what we're doing." McVay added that the Rams will nevertheless "work in collaboration and coordination with both the legal system and the league to be able to get all the necessary information to be able to listen and understand, and then ultimately be able to try to influence and affect positive decisions and use all these things as learning opportunities for us." Jackson previously was suspended two games under the Personal Conduct Policy for a different situation. That becomes an aggravating factor for a second suspension, which could make it longer than the baseline ban of six games for domestic violence. Jackson, 28, has been a full-time starter since 2023. He has a base salary of $18.925 million in 2026, with $1.45 million in per-game roster bonuses.
author: Mike Florio

title: Given the limits of the acclimation period, the NFLPA will check video of Nic Scourton ACL tear
summary: Season-ending injuries are one of the constant risks of training camp, and Panthers linebacker Nic Scourton experienced one on the first day of 2026 practice.
full_text: ' Season-ending injuries are one of the constant risks of training camp, and Panthers linebacker Nic Scourton experienced one on the first day of 2026 practice. Scourton suffered an ACL tear on a field that reporters have characterized as wet. Given that the first five days of camp are supposed to be an "acclimation period," the outcome merits closer scrutiny. Per a source with knowledge of the situation, the NFL Players Association will review video of the practice to understand the circumstances. If it was a non-contact fluke, that's one thing. If the Panthers were straying beyond the limits of the acclimation period, it's another. Article 23 of the Collective Bargaining Agreement contains general rules regarding the five-day, on-field acclimation period. Article 23, Section 7(a) provides that "[t]he first day of a Club’s preseason training camp shall be limited to physical examinations, meetings, and classroom instruction; no on-field activities shall be permitted other than running and conditioning.” The on-field work is “limited to Phase One-type conditioning, timing and testing, except that all coaches are permitted on the field.” On days two through five, no live contact is permitted, with only helmets and protective shirts permitted during one of the two practices each day. The video of the practice will reveal plenty as to how the injury happened, and whether the specific conditions complied with the limits of the acclimation period.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jets place DL T'Vondre Sweat on the active/non-football injury list
summary: The Jets made three moves on Saturday ahead of the start of training camp next week.
full_text: ' The Jets made three moves on Saturday ahead of the start of training camp next week. They included placing defensive lineman T'Vondre Sweat on the active/non-football injury list. Zack Rosenblatt of TheAthletic.com reports that Sweat has a minor hamstring injury that is not expected to keep him sidelined long. The acquisition of Sweat, in a trade with the Titans, was one of the team's key offseason moves. Sweat totaled 34 tackles and two sacks last season. The Jets placed wide receiver Tim Patrick and defensive end Tyler Baron on the active/physically unable to perform list. Baron is working his way back from a knee injury that ended his rookie season in Week 14 last season. He appeared in six games in 2025, playing 95 defensive snaps and 35 special teams snaps and recorded nine tackles, including a tackle for loss. Patrick, whose injury is undisclosed, signed with the Jets in May after appeared in 16 games for the Jaguars last season. He totaled 15 receptions for 187 yards and three touchdowns in 2025.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears place CB Kyler Gordon on active/PUP and T.J. Edwards on NFI
summary: Bears slot cornerback Kyler Gordon played only three games last season, twice landing on injured reserve.
full_text: '' Bears slot cornerback Kyler Gordon played only three games last season, twice landing on injured reserve. He will start the team's training camp on active/physically unable to perform. Gordon, who signed a three-year, $40 million extension in April 2025, battled groin, hamstring and calf injuries last season and his injury problems continued into the offseason program. A reported soft-tissue injury forced Gordon off the field during some of the team's offseason work. The Bears made several other moves Saturday, including placing linebacker T.J. Edwards on the non-football injury list. He fractured a fibula in the postseason but had returned to practice in the offseason program. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Edwards has a minor muscle strain that isn't expected to sideline him long. Linebacker Keyshaun Elliott (quad), linebacker Noah Sewell (Achilles), offensive lineman Ozzy Trapilo (left knee) and defensive lineman Shemar Turner (knee) joined Gordon on the active/PUP list.
author: Charean Williams

title: Patriots second-round LB Gabe Jacas agrees to terms
summary: Second-round linebacker Gabe Jacas did not report to training camp with his Patriots' teammates on Friday.
full_text: ' Second-round linebacker Gabe Jacas did not report to training camp with his Patriots' teammates on Friday. Jacas' holdout was short-lived, however. He agreed to terms on a four-year, $8.6 million contract on Saturday, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report. Jacas' signing will complete the Patriots' draft class signings. Jacas underwent arthroscopic surgery on a knee during the offseason, missing all of the team's offseason work. He will have some catching up to do when he is cleared to practice. The Patriots traded up in the second round to select Jacas 55th overall. The Illinois product totaled 11 sacks, 13.5 tackles for loss, and three forced fumbles last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: DL Omarr Norman-Lott, TE John Michael Gyllenborg begin Chiefs' camp on active/PUP
summary: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and wide receiver Rashee Rice are cleared to participate in the opening of training camp.
full_text: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and wide receiver Rashee Rice are cleared to participate in the opening of training camp. Rookie tight end John Michael Gyllenborg and second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott are not. Gyllenborg and Norman-Lott were placed on the active/physically unable to perform list on Saturday. The players can move back onto the 90-player roster once they have passed a physical. Norman-Lott tore the ACL in his right knee during a Week 7 game against the Raiders last season. He joined the team as a second-round pick in 2025 In five games as a rookie, Norman-Lott made five tackles and a sack. Gyllenborg, who signed with the Chiefs as an undrafted free agent earlier this year, is working through a knee sprain that kept him out of the offseason program.
author: Charean Williams

title: Matthew Stafford will have a reduced practice schedule to keep him fresh
summary: Last year, after Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford didn't practice much in training camp due to a back problem, outsiders incorrectly assumed that coach Sean McVay was giving Stafford a break.
full_text: ' Last year, after Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford didn't practice much in training camp due to a back problem, outsiders incorrectly assumed that coach Sean McVay was giving Stafford a break. This year, McVay is giving Stafford a break. Via Sarah Barshop of ESPN, McVay said that Stafford will not practice on the first and third days of the Rams' four-day training-camp practice blocks. The goal, said McVay, will be to keep Stafford "fresh and ready to go" for Week 1. At times last August, it appeared that Stafford wouldn't be ready to go for Week 1. He ultimately played the whole year, had one of the best seasons of his career, and won his first NFL MVP award. So, no, he doesn't need a full slate of practice reps. In turn, Stafford's potential backups do. With no veteran option (for now), Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett need the work. And with Jimmy Garoppolo suddenly talking about playing again, the Rams may decide that they need to get him to come back for another season as QB2 in L.A.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers expect Kyle Shanahan to be cleared from concussion long before season opener
summary: The 49ers held their opening news conference Saturday, and General Manager John Lynch was conspicuously alone on the podium.
full_text: ' The 49ers held their opening news conference Saturday, and General Manager John Lynch was conspicuously alone on the podium. The team announced earlier in the day that coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car wreck that left him with serious injuries, including a concussion. "Here's the great news: It looks like everyone’s doing all right ," Lynch said, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "The other driver seems to be doing all right. I don't want to speak to that, because that's just second-hand knowledge. Kyle is doing good. He's got some bumps and bruises. He did suffer a concussion in the accident, has some lingering effects from that concussion. "We don't have a protocol for staff members when it comes to concussions, but we do with players, and it's become very helpful. So, Kyle basically is going to be in the protocol, and [Dr. Anthony "Nino" Saglimbeni] and all the great doctors we have are giving him great care, and we're going to let the condition, the doctors dictate how he comes back, when he comes back." Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs and his hand, and he required 40 stitches to his face following the July 14 accident. He also was diagnosed with a severe concussion following the collision with an SUV near his California home. Shanahan, who has visited the team facility since the wreck, is expected to have a limited role to start camp that could include attending some practices. Offensive line coach and assistant head coach Chris Foerster handling the head coaching responsibilities until Shanahan returns. "He's a tremendous head coach, but this is bigger than that," Lynch said. "This is about his well-being, and we're going to take the time necessary. I think we're very equipped to do that." Shanahan should be cleared in plenty of time for the season opener against the Rams in Australia. "I think the expectation is that, long before that, he'll be better," Lynch said. "But again, everybody responds to these things differently, and we're going to do whatever it takes to have him right when he comes back, and it's the right thing to do."
author: Charean Williams

title: Bengals place DL B.J. Hill on PUP list
summary: The Bengals are set to open up training camp without defensive tackle B.J.
full_text: '' The Bengals are set to open up training camp without defensive tackle B.J. Hill on the field. The team announced on Saturday that Hill has been placed on the physically unable to perform list. Hill, who has an undisclosed injury, is eligible to come off that list at any point during camp, but won't be eligible to practice until he's off the list. Hill started every game for the Bengals last season and posted 66 tackles, five tackles for loss and four sacks. The Bengals also placed tight end Josh Kattus on the non-football injury list. Kattus signed with the Bengals after going undrafted out of Kentucky.
author: Josh Alper

title: George Kittle lands on PUP list to open 49ers camp
summary: There's been optimism about tight end George Kittle playing in Week 1 after tearing his Achilles in January, but he's not quite ready to practice yet. 49ers General Manager John Lynch said on Saturday that Kittle will be placed on the physically unable list to open training camp.
full_text: ' There's been optimism about tight end George Kittle playing in Week 1 after tearing his Achilles in January, but he's not quite ready to practice yet. 49ers General Manager John Lynch said on Saturday that Kittle will be placed on the physically unable list to open training camp. Lynch said that the team is happy with the progress that Kittle is making and that the tight end is doing "everything possible" to play in Week 1 against the Rams in Melbourne. Defensive end Mykel Williams (ACL), defensive tackle Alfred Collins (shoulder), and running back Isaac Guerendo (pectoral) are also going to be placed on the PUP list. Defensive end Nick Bosa (ACL) and linebacker Fred Warner (ankle) will not go on the list, which bodes well for their fitness heading into the season. Lynch also said that the 49ers will sign tight end Tanner McLachlan. McLachlan played in two games for the Bengals in 2024 and spent time on the Chargers' practice squad last season. The team will waive defensive tackle Evan Anderson and tight end Khalil Dinkins in other roster moves this weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cardinals activate Paris Johnson off the PUP list
summary: After the Cardinals placed left tackle Paris Johnson on the physically unable to perform list this week, head coach Mike LaFleur said that he was dealing with a minor knee injury and would be "back before you know it."
full_text: '' After the Cardinals placed left tackle Paris Johnson on the physically unable to perform list this week, head coach Mike LaFleur said that he was dealing with a minor knee injury and would be " back before you know it ." LaFleur was proven correct on Saturday. The Cardinals announced that Johnson has been activated from the PUP list. The move clears Johnson to begin taking part in practices with the team. Johnson, who has started all 43 games he's played since being drafted in the first round in 2023, is eligible for a contract extension this offseason. Linebacker Josh Sweat remains on the PUP list. Sweat missed most of the team's offseason program, but LaFleur said the move was "just maintenance" and that he has not picked up on any unhappiness from the team's top pass rusher.
author: Josh Alper

title: John Lynch on Brandon Aiyuk: We're focused on players that are here
summary: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has had a lot to say this offseason about his desire to play for the Commanders, but the 49ers have not released him and General Manager John Lynch did not make it sound like that is going to happen in the immediate future when he spoke to reporters from the team's training camp on Saturday.
full_text: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has had a lot to say this offseason about his desire to play for the Commanders, but the 49ers have not released him and General Manager John Lynch did not make it sound like that is going to happen in the immediate future when he spoke to reporters from the team's training camp on Saturday. Aiyuk did not play at all last season and the 49ers placed him on the reserve/left squad list in December after voiding the remaining guarantees on his contract earlier in the year. That move came because Aiyuk did not rehab a knee injury with the team and he has said that he won't move for reinstatement because he refuses to do "any business" with the club. Doing so would force the 49ers to make a decision about cutting him loose, but the status quo leaves the 49ers with little reason to make a move and Lynch said that he's going to keep his attention on players that are still with the team. “Brandon is on a left squad designation," Lynch said. "As such, he’s not on our 90-man roster. I, personally, and we as an organization, are going to focus on the players that are here. I don’t have anything to add to that. We wish him well. We wish his family well.” The 49ers play the Commanders in Week 6, but it doesn't look like Aiyuk will be playing for anybody in that contest or any other unless he decides on a different course of action in the near future.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ty Simpson agrees to rookie deal with Rams
summary: Rams quarterback Ty Simpson started the day as the only 2026 first-round pick without a contract, but that is set to change.
full_text: ' Rams quarterback Ty Simpson started the day as the only 2026 first-round pick without a contract, but that is set to change. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Simpson has agreed to his four-year rookie deal with the NFC West club. Simpson will make $25.4 million under the terms of the deal and the Rams will hold an option for a fifth season. Simpson, who was the 13th overall pick this year, is set to compete with Stetson Bennett for the backup job behind Matthew Stafford. Now that Simpson has agreed to his deal, Patriots second-round pick Gabe Jacas is the only unsigned player from the entire 2026 draft class. Jacas has been dealing with injuries and did not report to Patriots training camp this week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders put Dorance Armstrong, Deatrich Wise on PUP list
summary: The Commanders announced a handful of roster moves before the start of their training camp this week.
full_text: ' The Commanders announced a handful of roster moves before the start of their training camp this week. Defensive ends Dorance Armstrong and Deatrich Wise have both been placed on the physically unable to perform list. Armstrong suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 7 of the 2025 season while Wise went down with a quad injury in Week 2. Cornerback Trey Amos was also placed on the PUP list. He fractured his fibula in Week 10 last year. The Commanders rounded out the day's moves by placing undrafted rookie cornerback Fred Davis II on the non-football illness list. All four players still count against the 90-man roster limit and they can be activated at any point during camp.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean McVay: Aaron Donald is putting himself in position to make a decision
summary: Donald is weighing whether or not he will come out of retirement for the 2026 season.
full_text: ' The Rams are starting training camp without defensive tackle Aaron Donald on the roster, but the prospect of his return from retirement is still a point of great interest. Donald has been mulling a return after two years away from the game so that he can play with new Ram Myles Garrett and head coach Sean McVay was asked about where things stand during his first press conference of the summer. McVay said that the Rams are in contact with Donald and taking it "a day at a time" because Donald is still figuring out if he's physically up for getting back on the field. "He is going through his process," McVay said. "He is putting himself in a position to make a decision and he’s earned the right to be able to do that. . . . If that is something he wants to do, we’re going to try to make that happen." If Donald does decide to return, there's been speculation that it might not be for the start of the season. McVay was asked about that possibility as well. "He’s gonna go through what he’s going through right now," McVay said. "We’ll see how his body’s responding to some of the training and the way he puts himself through the paces to know what it looks and feels like to take on what the rigors of an NFL season entail. If he’s feeling good about that, we’ll move forward and what those dates are I’ll share when we have more information." McVay said that he has no doubt that Donald will be "ready to rock" if he decides to move forward with resuming his playing career, but it looks like it will be at least a little while before we know which way the three-time defensive player of the year is going to go.
author: Josh Alper

title: Panthers sign three players, cut three others
summary: The Panthers had several players in for workouts on Friday and that led to some roster shuffling on Saturday.
full_text: ' The Panthers had several players in for workouts on Friday and that led to some roster shuffling on Saturday. They announced that they have signed defensive tackle Kyon Barrs, defensive tackle Elijah Garcia, and cornerback DeCarlos Nicholson to their 90-man roster. Offensive tackle Derrell Bailey, linebacker Jared Bartlett, and cornerback Mike Reid were waived in corresponding moves. Garcia is the only new arrival with NFL regular season experience. He has played in 17 games for the Broncos, Giants and Falcons over the last four seasons. He has 28 tackles, two sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery Barrs has spent time with the Seahawks and Cardinals while Nicholson was briefly on the Browns after going undrafted this April.
author: Josh Alper

title: Robert Kraft: We've offered to make Christian Gonzalez the top-paid cornerback
summary: Cornerback Christian Gonzalez is at Patriots training camp as he continues to talk to the team about a contract extension and Saturday brought some idea of what those conversations have looked like this offseason.
full_text: Cornerback Christian Gonzalez is at Patriots training camp as he continues to talk to the team about a contract extension and Saturday brought some idea of what those conversations have looked like this offseason. Patriots owner Robert Kraft said that the team has offered Gonzalez a deal that would set records for both NFL cornerbacks and members of the Patriots organization. "We love Christian Gonzalez. We love him as a player, as a person, and that's why we've made an offer to him to make him the highest-paid player to ever play that position in the NFL," Kraft said, via Mike Reiss of ESPN.com. "And coincidentally, it is the highest contract in Patriots franchise history. So we're glad we drafted him, he's developed here, and we hope he'll be with us for a long time." Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie set the bar at the position when he signed a four-year, $124 million deal this offseason. A recent report indicated that Gonzalez's negotiations have been complicated by the Seahawks' ongoing talks with Devon Witherspoon. The cornerbacks share an agent and Witherspoon, who is also shooting for the top of the market for corners, is reportedly closer to an agreement that could open the door for the Patriots and Gonzalez reaching the finish line.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jordyn Brooks is at the center of the Dolphins' cultural change
summary: The Dolphins have torn apart their roster in an effort to build a team.
full_text: The Dolphins have torn apart their roster in an effort to build a team. One important holdover could be the key to changing the culture. Linebacker Jordyn Brooks. He's the player who had no qualms about calling the team " soft " after a 2024 Thanksgiving night embarrassment at Lambeau Field. He was even more candid about the past, present, and future in a recent conversation with Tyler Dunne of GoLongTD.com. “If the team is playing soft, we’re playing soft,” Brooks told Dunne. “We’re not playing the way that we should be playing. Let’s call it what it is. We’re getting killed out here in the cold. We’re fitting right into the narrative. As a leader, that’s what you’re supposed to do.” The issue with the Dolphins of recent years was a lack of true leadership from their supposed leaders. “I don’t think you can be a leader because somebody says you are one,” Brooks told Dunne. “It’s a natural instinct — and people go about it in different ways — but it’s a natural instinct to get something done: No, we’ve got to get it done. . . . “It came to a point where I realized, ‘OK, some of these guys aren’t serious about this, and we are suffering behind it. I can’t just sit here and just let it go by. Showing up late to meetings. Not buying into what we’re trying to do. We play football. If enough guys are not all the way locked in, we’re going to suffer. Basketball team, 15 guys, it’s a lot easier to get everybody to buy in. Whoever isn’t bought in is going to stick out like a sore thumb. But it’s easier to hide when it’s 50, 60 guys.” The team's struggles in the cold weren't the disease. They were the symptom. Miami's Super Bowl-winning teams of 50-plus years ago won wherever, whenever. In whatever conditions they faced. During our offseason interviews with new coach Jeff Hafley and new G.M. Jon-Eric Sullivan, that message was unmistakable. It's not about finding players who can play in the cold. It's about finding players who can play under all types of weather. Under any type of circumstances. That's the culture they're trying to instill. And Brooks was, by all appearances, the outlier in recent years. Now, he could be the lightning rod. “My true value is to be a leader of men,” Brooks said. “We’ve got a bunch of rookies. I’ve got a lot of knowledge that I can give them through my own experience that can help them be more successful. That’s my true value. . . . I went through all those lows for these moments.” The Dolphins will be relying heavily on young, cheap players in 2026 (and 2027), thanks to the massive financial consequences of the disastrous market-is-the-market contract given to former starting quarterback Tua Tagovailoa. (The Dolphins will pay him more than $50 million this year to play for the Falcons.) Brooks believes the culture change can change everything. “I know a lot of people look at it like, ‘Man, I’m not trying to be part of no rebuild,'" Brooks said. "But look at it the right way. Nobody said a rebuild has to be three years. It can be three months. They drafted a lot of great dudes that are going to be stars in the league. . . . Who knows man? The Miami Dolphins might surprise a lot of people this year.” It's not just idle talk. Brooks can feel the difference. “A lot of people on the outside are going to look at our team and be like, ‘Yeah, 0-17,’” Brooks said. “But me? When you’re in it, it’s different. You never have that mindset. I understand why people would say the things they say. ‘How many stars do they have? Proven guys?’ We ain’t got a lot of them. But we tried that and it didn’t work. To me, this is exactly what we need. Whatever the vision is, I’m all-in. The best teams win. Not the best players.” He's right. Great teams perform in a way that allows specific players to be perceived as great. With 10 teammates on the field, it's very hard for one player to stand out, if the other 10 aren't fully committed. Commitment was the issue in the past. Dunne's article includes comments from unnamed former Dolphins players who painted a troubling picture about the attitude of some of the team's captains. The status apparently was based on past production, not true leadership. “Nobody respected the guys with the Cs on their chest, because they didn’t give a fuck," an unnamed player told Dunne. "They made some crazy plays. Jalen [Ramsey] is one of the most talented, gifted athletes I’ve ever seen. Obviously, Tyreek [Hill] is. But other young players follow them. And watch them. And see how they do things.” If players see enough of certain things, they'll get to the point where they've seen enough. “We didn’t fight for each other on the field,” a former Dolphins player told Dunne. “We just didn’t give a fuck. Offense didn’t care about the defense. Defense didn’t care about the offense. That’s how it went. I stopped giving a fuck.” Dunne's article places plenty of blame on former coach Mike McDaniel. An offensive starter said McDaniel “was just too much of a bro” and lost control of the locker room. McDaniel tried to get things under control after G.M. Chris Grier was fired and McDaniel was given a chance to save his whistle. He benched Tagovailoa after a Monday night loss in Pittsburgh. By then, it was too late. The Dolphins needed a full reset. The most encouraging sign moving forward is the presence of a G.M. and head coach who are fully aligned. That limits the possibility of dysfunction settling in once adversity arrives. And if they've made the right decisions as to the players they've dropped, the players they've kept, and the players they've added, the perpetually underachieving collection of stars could be replaced by a group of unknown players who will become stars if the collection of them performs like a team.

title: Kyle Shanahan suffered "severe concussion" and other injuries in July 14 car accident

full_text: ' The 49ers have announced that coach Kyle Shanahan was recently involved in a car accident. Per the release, the accident happened last week. Shanahan suffered " non-life-threatening injuries ." He'll participate in team activities "on a limited basis" at the start of training camp while he recovers. Assistant head coach Chris Foerster will handle the head-coaching responsibilities during this period of time. ESPN reports that "Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs, his hand, needed over 40 stitches in his face and suffered a severe concussion " during the July 14 accident that occurred near his home in California. His car collided with an SUV. The other driver was not injured. No one has been cited for the accident, and the authorities have said alcohol or drugs were not involved. Shanahan was treated and released at a local hospital. He has been recovering at home. Doctors have declined to clear him to participate in all training-camp practices until the concussion symptoms subside. He's starting his tenth season as head coach of the 49ers. title: Bill Belichick wants NCAA and NFL playing rules to be standardized
summary: After 50 years in the NFL, Bill Belichick is starting his second season as a college coach.
full_text: ' After 50 years in the NFL, Bill Belichick is starting his second season as a college coach. He'd like to harmonize the playing rules at the two levels of football. “You watch multiple games on Saturday and see one set of rules,” Belichick said Friday at the National Football Foundation’s Bill Dooley Chapter Pigskin Preview, via Kamran Nia of the Raleigh News & Observer . “And you turn on the game on Sunday, and you have a different set of rules .” Differences in pro and college rules have existed for decades. Most notably, receivers at the college level only need to get one foot in bounds to make a catch. In the NFL, it's two. Likewise, defensive pass interference is a 15-yard penalty in college football. It's a spot foul in the NFL. More recently, the NFL's embrace of the electric-football kickoff has yet to be incorporated into the college game. There are other differences, when it comes to clock management. Only last year did college football add a two-minute warning, but with a less ominous term. One one hand, it won't take much to iron out the differences. On the other hand, the differences don't significantly change the nature of the game. Football is still football, even with some variations. It's unlikely the NFL will adjust its rules to mirror college football. If the NCAA wants to better prepare players, coaches, and officials for the highest level of the sport, it's for the NCAA to choose to do it. Regardless, there has rarely been a clamoring for one set of rules. Would it be easier if the rules were the same? Sure. But it's an issue that is rarely if ever raised. Now that Belichick has, we'll see if his stated preference gets any traction.

title: The latest LeBron James decision highlights the reality of inside information in sports
summary: The intersection of sports and gambling has created the very real risk of inside information being harvested and utilized to give bettors an edge.
full_text: The intersection of sports and gambling has created the very real risk of inside information being harvested and utilized to give bettors an edge. Throw in the ever-growing prediction markets, and the folks who know things as part of their jobs have real power. The recent LeBron James guessing game illustrates how a world of unregulated inside information can move markets, and can allow some to make money. Consider the Miami Heat social-media snafu that resulted in the Miami Heat leaking news of an upcoming introductory press conference. Even if it was a mistake (Schefty was pushing the idea of LeBron to Miami in a Thursday appearance on radio in Philly), some of the people who saw it or heard about it surely placed wagers that James would sign with the Heat. (And, if they did, they lost.) Then there's the issue of having personal access to one of the top insiders covering a given sport. With ESPN's Shams Charania currently the preeminent NBA insider, he was in a position to either know exactly what was going to happen — or to have a pretty good inkling. As the Ryan Gold situation possibly demonstrates, there are degrees of inside information. Even if someone doesn't know what's going to happen with certainty, certain people are in position to know more than the general public does. And no one seems to be paying attention. No one seems to care. It's the Wild West age of wagering, with many simply focusing on stuffing as much money in their pockets as possible, without regard to the broader societal consequences. Or the reckoning that they may personally experience, if/when an ambitious federal prosecutor convenes a grand jury to take a closer look at whether and to what extent those who have this kind of sensitive information are mishandling it.

title: Former NFL offensive lineman Jordan Devey dies at 38
summary: Jordan Devey, who played for five NFL teams over eight years, has died.
full_text: Jordan Devey, who played for five NFL teams over eight years, has died. He was 38. Via Jeremy Tombs of Fox 13 in Salt Lake City, Devey died by suicide. His parents told Tombs that they believe Devey suffered from CTE. Undrafted in 2013 out of Memphis, Devey initially signed with the Ravens but was released. He landed on the Patriots' roster in 2013 and 2014, winning a Super Bowl ring to cap his second year in New England. Devey spent 2015 with the 49ers, 2016 through 2018 with the Chiefs, 2019 with the Raiders, and 2020 with the Bills. He appeared in 44 regular-season games with 21 starts. We extend our condolences to Devey's family, friends, teammates and coaches.

title: Kyle Shanahan injured in car accident: 49ers coach to begin training camp in limited role
summary: Reports say Shanahan suffered a broken nose, three broken ribs, a broken hand, a concussion and required more than 40 stitches to his face after the July 14 crash
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have officially reported to training camp but will begin building the foundation for the 2026 campaign with their head coach limited. The team announced in a statement Saturday that Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week and suffered non-life-threatening injuries.
Shanahan, 46, will still participate in team activities, but on a limited basis. Assistant head coach Chris Foerster and the team coordinators will handle the bulk of the head coach duties while Shanahan recuperates. In a press conference on Saturday, 49ers general manager John Lynch told reporters that he does not expect Shanahan to miss Week 1 of the regular season.
Here is the full official statement from the 49ers:
"San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week where he suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers. Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care.
Assistant Head Coach Chris Foerster along with team coordinators will handle head coach responsibilities during this period."
The accident occurred July 14 when Shanahan collided with an SUV near his Northern California home, per ESPN . While the injuries weren't life-threatening, they were significant. ESPN reported that Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs and his hand, suffered a severe concussion and needed more than 40 stitches to his face.
Shanahan was taken by paramedics to a local hospital and released later that day. The other driver was not injured, according to Palo Alto Lt. Nicholas Martinez. He also told ESPN that drugs and alcohol were not involved, and both drivers cooperated with law enforcement.
Since the crash, Shanahan has been recovering at home and informed the coaching staff of the incident Tuesday. He has yet to be cleared by doctors for full coaching duties and won't be until his concussion symptoms subside.
Shanahan is entering his 10th season as the 49ers' head coach. Since being hired in 2017, he has become one of the league's top coaches, compiling an 82-67 (.550) regular-season record and a 9-5 playoff mark. Under his leadership, San Francisco has made two Super Bowl appearances and is coming off a 12-5 regular-season campaign in 2025 that ended with a divisional-round loss to the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks .
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Jordan Devey dies at 38: Family says former NFL guard died by suicide
summary: Devey played seven NFL seasons with five teams, winning Super Bowl XLIX with the Patriots
full_text:
Jordan Devey , a former NFL guard and Super Bowl champion, has died at the age of 38. A GoFundMe established after his death to help support Devey's family says he died by suicide.
"Tragically, Jordan took his own life, leaving his family to navigate an incredibly difficult and heartbreaking time," the GoFundMe page reads.
Speaking with Fox 13 in Salt Lake City , Devey's mother, Leslie, said the family believes he "possibly suffered from CTE." However, the family said it will not be able to test for the neurodegenerative disease due to the nature of his death.
Following his death, Devey's wife, Lindsay, posted a photo of the offensive lineman in his hospital bed on what would've been their 15th wedding anniversary.
"We have filled the walls of our homes and hearts with countless memories, joys, struggles, and triumphs," Lindsay's Instagram post reads . "We brought 4 beautiful children into this world that have your eyes, freckles, and compassion. You were our hero and our hearts ache in your absence. We love you. We miss you. And as you said in your last words to me, 'we'll talk soon.'"
pic.twitter.com/tSyYejM8nO
Devey began his NFL career by signing with the Baltimore Ravens in 2013 as an undrafted free agent out of Memphis. After spending the offseason with Baltimore, he joined the New England Patriots ' practice squad in early September. In 2014, he saw his first regular-season action, playing in seven games with four starts as New England went on to win Super Bowl XLIX.
The Patriots traded Devey to the San Francisco 49ers in the summer of 2015, where he saw the most playing time of his career. He appeared in 15 games with nine starts at guard. The Utah native then spent three seasons (2016-18) with the Kansas City Chiefs before finishing his career with the Las Vegas Raiders (2019) and Buffalo Bills (2020). In all, he appeared in 44 regular-season games with 21 starts.

full_text: A lot of players come and go in the NFL. Usually when they hang up their cleats, it is because their roster options have dried up and their agent’s phone stopped ringing. Not true for Travis Vokolek, a former Arizona Cardinals tight end. He is retiring at the age of 28 due to a serious neck injury he suffered last year in Week 6 on the road against the Indianapolis Colts, according to Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com . RELATED: TRAINING CAMP TIGHT END OUTLOOK In the play, Vokolek was pushed by Colts linebacker Segun Olubi on a kickoff. Vokolek then landed wrong and hit the ground awkwardly. The stretcher was summoned with both of his arms strapped down, and was taken off the field via the medical cart. He was listed on the depth chart as the TE3 who had duties on special teams mainly. He did have some offensive time in four of the first five games of the 2025 season. He ended the year with 32 offensive snaps and 45 special teams plays. Vololek played for the Cardinals for three seasons. View this post on Instagram Vololek gave a detailed description of his football life on Instagram, and what led to his decision to retire from professional football. He ended up on IR, one of 24 rostered players who found this list their new home, and the Cardinals did not tender him a contract this offseason, making him a free agent. After a decent college career at Nebraska, he was not selected in the 2023 NFL draft and then signed with the Baltimore Ravens. He was a last-day cut, then signed to their practice squad. Later in the season, the Cardinals claimed him off Baltimore’s practice squad after an injury to Geoff Swaim. He made Arizona’s roster in both the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

title: Sights and sounds from Cardinals’ Friday training camp
summary: Several NFL clubs have gotten their rookies into a training camp surrounding on Friday. Yawn. The entire roster for the Arizona Cardinals are way ahead of them. Training camp is what separates the men from the boys, the players versus the future real estate agents, and what the franchise can expect going into this year’s […]
full_text: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew II (15) leads a huddle during training camp at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on July 23, 2026. | Patrick Breen/The Republic / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Several NFL clubs have gotten their rookies into a training camp surrounding on Friday. Yawn. The entire roster for the Arizona Cardinals are way ahead of them. Training camp is what separates the men from the boys, the players versus the future real estate agents, and what the franchise can expect going into this year’s schedule. Keep in mind, Arizona has a preseason game against the Carolina Panthers on August 6 in the Hall of Fame Game situated in Canton, Ohio. RELATED: NEWS FROM CARDINALS TRAINING CAMP On Friday, fans were permitted to watch practices, and unlike a lot of NFL teams, the tickets were no charge. Don’t you hate it when teams want more out of fans? A lot of bodies in the media area were on hand as well. Right now, it’s just lids and shorts. Although the offensive line is lined up, and a mock defensive line is also lined up and “acting” like they are rushing, the main focus is to know what to do and where to be along the offensive line on a called play. However, on passing plays, the receivers are giving it all they’ve got, and not a single DB wants guys catching balls in front of them. Which means good effort from both position groups so far. It is also giving the offensive coaches an idea of which receivers are getting their routes correct, and which ones are lost. View this post on Instagram QB Gardner Minshew tossed the ball all around the yard today. His fav so far was Marvin Harrison, who is looking good and seems to have bulked up a bit, but he also likes TE Trey McBride, who made a highlight play. QB Carson Beck has shown that if Jacoby Brissett isn’t getting this new offense down, he is already making an argument to become the Week 1 starter. The dude can slice it into a narrow window and has a strong arm with great velocity. Understandably, there isn’t much of a pass rush; we get that. And nobody on either side of the line is pushing the staying power of their deodorant. He is simply making a statement that the QB3 label and waiting a year may be for somebody else. He especially looks solid rolling out and looking for an open man downfield. All four quarterbacks were seen throwing. Minshew and Beck were getting the first-team reps so far. Kedon Slovis was active as well and had the day’s only turnover, a fumble. Whether that’s just early camp or the way it is going to be will be determined. But if the Cardinals had a game tomorrow, it would be Minshew under center with Beck holding the tablet. View this post on Instagram Brissett also looks a bit sluggish and may even have a bit more weight on him. Haven’t seen or heard about him being weighed, and maybe it’s the black jersey all QBs are wearing, but he isn’t fluid with his movements at all so far. Lots of passes thrown during receiver drills without any front line. Rookie WR Reggie Virgil is running some good routes and has moves. The defensive backs are in a quandary so far. While there isn’t any real hitting, which would cause some dropped balls via a good pop here and there, plus the receivers know where they are going, the defensive back group is proving to be very aggressive. CB Max Melton has popped out a few balls along with CBs Jaden Davis and Will Johnson. If S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson batted away one ball, he batted away six or seven. LB Jordan Burch seems to be getting to know where in coverage he must end up. S Budda Baker was intermingled with his safety group and looked more like the safety group coach than a player. He was seen very active with the younger guys as well as veteran Andrew Wingard. There are seven safeties in camp, and most likely the team will only keep four. Five may make it if DC Nick Rallis decides to use more 4-2-5 this year. And really, the defense did much better than the offense. Which is normal early on. But it’s not the defensive backfield that’s under the microscope during camp; it’s this new offense. Oddly enough, on the Isaiah Adams front, he was at camp taking part in drills. It was not known what his recent weapons arrest would do for him being available. The next open practices are Sunday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and next Friday again.

title: Ravens place Nnamdi Madubuike, Travis Jones and others on PUP list
summary: On Saturday evening, the Ravens officially placed defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list, as reported by The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebeic. In addition to Madbuike, they also placed several other players on the PUP list: DT Travis Jones, ILB Teddye Buchanan, CB Bilhal Kone, DT John Jenkins, and OLB Adisa […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - JANUARY 11: Nnamdi Madubuike #92 of the Baltimore Ravens lines up before the snap during an NFL football wild card playoff game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at M&T Bank Stadium on January 11, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Saturday evening, the Ravens officially placed defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list, as reported by The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebeic . In addition to Madbuike, they also placed several other players on the PUP list: DT Travis Jones, ILB Teddye Buchanan, CB Bilhal Kone, DT John Jenkins, and OLB Adisa Isaac, all for varying different injuries. The update on Madubuike is most notable, as fans have been long awaiting news on the status of the All-Pro in his recovery from a neck injury. While the PUP list sometimes indicates a player will be sidelined for an extended period of time, this does not appear to be the case for Madubuike. According to Zrebiec, Madubuike has been cleared to return to football action by independent spine and cervical doctors — a significant hurdle that at least ensures he can ultimately take the field again. Ever since Madubuike suffered a season-ending neck injury in 2025, there’s been a looming cloud of uncertainty as to whether or not he may ever play again. Zrebiec also added that the 28-year-old is on PUP for the team to evaluate his conditioning state and could begin practicing as early as next week. Madubuike’s return to action would be a huge boost for the Ravens’ defense, as he’s the team’s best interior pass rusher. He racked up 54 pressures, 19.5 sacks and 50 quarterback hits in 2023 and 2024 combined. Jones, who had a career-best season in 2025, is returning from a pectoral injury but should also be set to take the field sooner rather than later. Jones stepped up as a leading defensive presence in Madubuike’s absence last year and earned a three-year contract extension. When Jones and Madubuike are both back in the fold, now joined by veteran Calais Campbell, the Ravens will have a much-improved defensive front. Buchanan suffered a torn ACL in the back-half of his 2025 season, which cut short a solid rookie campaign. He had seized the starting linebacker role opposite Roquan Smith and was named AFC Defensive Rookie of the Month in October. Buchanan’s recovery status will be worth watching, but the Ravens have a serviceable option to start in the meantime in Trenton Simpson. Perhaps the biggest disappointing PUP placement from this list is Isaac, who is entering a make-or-break summer. The former fourth-round pick has played only 32 total defensive snaps since being drafted in 2024 and has dealt with multiple injuries that have kept him sidelined. For Isaac to secure a roster spot and be able to carve out a role, a quick return to action from his elbow injury will be important.

title: Buffalo Bills announce new tailgate rules for stadium lots
summary: Fans of the Buffalo Bills knew the game day experience in the new Highmark Stadium could be different than what they were used to in the old Highmark Stadium/New Era Field/Ralph Wilson Stadium/Rich Stadium, which Buffalo called home from 1973 through 2025. That happens whenever a team ditches an old, familiar stadium for a new, […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - JANUARY 22: Buffalo Bills fans tailgate in the parking lot prior to the AFC Divisional Playoff game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on January 22, 2023 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fans of the Buffalo Bills knew the game day experience in the new Highmark Stadium could be different than what they were used to in the old Highmark Stadium/New Era Field/Ralph Wilson Stadium/Rich Stadium, which Buffalo called home from 1973 through 2025. That happens whenever a team ditches an old, familiar stadium for a new, state-of-the-art venue like Highmark Stadium, which will feature roughly 11,500 fewer seats with a higher cost of attending an NFL game than Bills fans were previously accustomed to. The changes are not limited to inside Highmark Stadium. Earlier this week, the team announced some new regulations for fans looking to tailgate in team-operated parking lots, including prohibiting the sale of food and drinks in their designated stadium parking lots, limiting the size and scope of fans tailgating areas, and cutting off all tailgating activities once kickoff has occurred. Which is a disappointing development for the fans who come out to the stadium for the sole purpose of living it up at a tailgate, even if they are not attending the game. Perhaps the rule that will irk the most Bills fans and go against the spirit of Bills’ tailgates? Fans may only bring food and beverages for their friends and family, and are not allowed to share their tasty tailgate treats with fellow Bills fans. Which is just a ridiculous clause to put into the policy, but don’t worry, later on in this article I will explain why this rule is null and void. Also worth noting: the Bills have had tailgating restrictions like these in place for years, but the rules have never been enforced before. In the tailgating rules shared on the Buffalo Bills website , fans “may bring and prepare food for consumption by their friends and family only,” and fans are not allowed to utilize private catering companies in the official team lots. For fans using the stadium lots for pregame tailgating, they are being limited to the available 9-feet by 10-feet tailgate space immediately behind their parked vehicle for all activities, including grilling food and playing games. View Link Megaphones, air horns and other noise-making items are not allowed for tailgating, and the same goes for tent poles or stakes that are driven into the ground. Looking to pump up your gameday crew with a lively playlist? Better make sure the lyrics are clean. The team says fans can bring in personal-sized speakers, but not larger speaker systems, and excessive volume is not permitted. The Bills are also asking their fans to treat the stadium lots like a campsite, adhering to a “carry out what you carry in” policy where all trash “must be disposed of in proper receptacles,” and “guests must return their area to its original state before entering the event. Trash bags must not be left beside a car or otherwise outside of a trash receptacle within the tailgating area. Here is the complete list of what is allowed and what is prohibited at these tailgates: Allowed Natural gas and propane grills Charcoal grills and open-fit fires that are raised at least six inches off the ground. Coals must be completely extinguished prior to entering the stadium and are not permitted to be dumped within Highmark Stadium parking lots. Plastic or non-breakable cups/cans Guests may bring and prepare food for consumption by their friends and family only. Personal-sized amplified sound system (e.g. small Bluetooth speaker) Bicycles are permitted in tailgating areas only at designated bike racks Prohibited Stakes, through-surface inserts (e.g. tent poles), anything driven into the ground Charcoal grills and open-pit fires that are not raised at least six inches off the ground. Wood stoves, oil fryers and/or other cooking stations. Bottles, glass containers Sale of food or beverage and private catering companies. Electrical cords cannot be placed across parking areas/drive aisles or in areas that would create a hazard for any guests. Portable public address systems are not permitted. Amplified sound systems cannot be used at excessive volumes, and playing music with inappropriate language (profanity, slurs, etc.) is prohibited. Non-licensed motorized and non-motorized vehicles are prohibited within the designated tailgating parking lot(s), including without limitation golf carts, Segways, skateboards, scooters, and hoverboards. Drones, remote-controlled unmanned aerial vehicles or other similar motorized vehicles/devices; possession or operation of such devices may result in immediate ejection from the site and may also result in confiscation of such devices by security and law enforcement. Megaphones, airhorns, and other noise making devices Selling of items or soliciting of any promotional or marketing activities Any item deemed inappropriate or dangerous to spectators, participants or Team Members. Weapons or firearms – this extends to both real weapons and fake weapons such as toy guns, swords, knives, hatchets or bombs that might be part of a costume As a reminder, these rules apply only to tailgating at a team-operated stadium lots, and won’t be instituted at the various private lots surrounding Highmark Stadium. While Bills fans will surely be left wondering how the team will enforce these rules at the new stadium, I do have one bit of good news to wrap up this story. As mentioned earlier, there’s a stipulation that states fans “may bring and prepare food for consumption by their friends and family only.” Luckily, Bills Mafia is the definition of family, so feel free to share your chicken wings, cheeseburgers, hot dogs, Italian sausages, pizza and other delicious tailgating fare with fellow Bills fans. As a longtime season ticket holder since 2007, I know I will still continue to treat our tailgates as the community-building activities they were meant to be, and will gladly share our food and drinks with Bills Mafia. What do you think about these new guidelines? Bills fans have rightfully earned a reputation as some of the best, most passionate tailgaters out there. Will these rules clash with the friendly, welcoming atmosphere that Bills Mafia has become known for? Be sure to leave your thoughts on these new guidelines in the comments section.

title: Bills news: Previewing Buffalo’s defensive backs
summary: The Buffalo Bills’ secondary features plenty of known talents like cornerback Christian Benford and safety Cole Bishop, but there are also a lot of question marks on the back of Buffalo’s defense as we prepare for the start of training camp. Who will start at CB2 opposite Benford? Can C.J. Gardner-Johnson provide stability as the […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills’ secondary features plenty of known talents like cornerback Christian Benford and safety Cole Bishop, but there are also a lot of question marks on the back of Buffalo’s defense as we prepare for the start of training camp. Who will start at CB2 opposite Benford? Can C.J. Gardner-Johnson provide stability as the starting safety alongside Bishop? How will second-year cornerback Maxwell Hairston develop following an injury-plagued rookie season? Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks attempts to answer some of those questions and leads off by previewing the state of Buffalo’s cornerbacks and safeties heading into the 2026 season. Check out the assessments and then be sure to leave your thoughts on how much talent is in Buffalo’s secondary in the comments section. The state of Buffalo’s defensive backs Christian Benford has proven himself to be one of the league’s best lockdown cover cornerbacks, while Cole Bishop enjoyed a breakthrough 2025 campaign and is expected to take another big step forward as a dynamic playmaker at the back of the defense. But beyond those two, there are plenty of questions in Buffalo’s secondary, a unit that saw plenty of turnover this offseason with the departure of nickel corner Taron Johnson, cornerback Tre’Davious White and safety Jordan Poyer. In their place, the Bills signed nickel corner Dee Alford and safeties C.J. Gardner-Johnson and Geno Stone in free agency, and drafted athletic Ohio State cornerback Davison Igbinosun and talented South Carolina safety Jalon Kilgore to shore up the secondary. We preview Buffalo’s cornerbacks—including breaking down the battle between Hairston and Igbinosun to claim the CB2 job—and dissect Buffalo’s safeties, including how Kilgore could wind up being the Bills long-term solution alongside Bishop and how fan-favorite Damar Hamlin enters training camp fighting for a spot on the 53-man roster. title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting report: guard O’Cyrus Torrence
summary: The Buffalo Bills have been remarkably consistent along the starting offensive line over the last few seasons. The Bills have, for the most part, started the same five players week in and week out. With a few exceptions, the team has been very healthy on the offensive line, and while they haven’t been so lucky […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 17: O'Cyrus Torrence #64 of the Buffalo Bills lines up before the snap during an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills have been remarkably consistent along the starting offensive line over the last few seasons. The Bills have, for the most part, started the same five players week in and week out. With a few exceptions, the team has been very healthy on the offensive line, and while they haven’t been so lucky at other positions, the people tasked with protecting Josh Allen have, fortunately, remained very healthy. One player in particular has been on the field more than anyone—including Allen—over the last three seasons. In today’s installment of “91 players in 91 days,” we discuss the Bills’ leader in offensive snaps last year. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: O’Cyrus Torrence Number: 64 Position: G Height/Weight: 6’5” 330 lbs. Age: 26 (27 on 1/20/2027) Experience/Draft: 4; selected by Buffalo in the second round (No. 59 overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft College: Florida Acquired: Second-round draft choice Financial situation (per Spotrac): Torrence enters the final yera of his four-year rookie contract. For the 2026 season, his cap hit is $4,305,087 if he’s on the 53-man roster. If Buffalo releases him, they’ll carry a dead cap charge of $381,087. 2025 Recap: Torrence once again played in all 17 games, and he started all 17 games for the second time in his three professional seasons. For the third consecutive season, Torrence played more snaps on offense than any Buffalo player, as well. If Pro Football Focus grades are your thing, he grades out as an average to slightly below-average guard, scoring a 59.8 overall in their grading system. That had him at No. 44 out of 81 qualifiers at the position. His pass block grade was a 64 (32nd out of 81 guards) and his run block grade was a 54.6 (58th out of 81 guards). He committed just one penalty and allowed three sacks on the year. Positional outlook: Torrence is one of five players whose sole position listed is guard. Ar’Maj Reed-Adams, Bruno Fina, Da’Metrius Weatherspoon, and Nick Broeker are the others. Alec Anderson, Connor McGovern, Austin Corbett, and Sedrick Van Pran-Granger are listed at center/guard, while Tylan Grable and Jude Bowry are listed at tackle/guard. 2026 Offseason: Torrence is healthy and he participated in offeseason workouts. 2026 Season outlook: The question for Buffalo isn’t whether Torrence will start at guard this year; instead, it’s whether this will be the last year where he starts at guard for the team. Spotrac has Torrence’s market value at $39 million over three years , and while general manager Brandon Beane has shown some salary cap wizardry in the past, it’s not out of the realm of possibility that Torrence will receive an offer from elsewhere on the free agent market that he can’t refuse. Will Beane look to lock him in before he hits free agency? That’s also a possibility, as an August extension is certainly something that the team could do. Has Torrence’s play justified a top-twenty guard’s salary? PFF says no, but if we’re being honest here—and honest is something I always strive to be—the analytics don’t match the eye test when I watch Torrence play. He does a nice job at the point of attack, he effectively communicates with Spencer Brown and Connor McGovern at right tackle and center, respectively, on pass protection, and he wins his reps more often than not. Frankly, he wouldn’t have led the team in offensive snaps over the last three years if he was as “mid” as the PFF numbers suggest that he is. Beane likely would have tried to replace him, and he already had someone on the roster that the team views as a capable lineman in Alec Anderson, who will battle for the left guard spot now that veteran David Edwards is off with the New Orleans Saints. For my money, O’Cyrus Torrence is a solid interior lineman who sometimes can be beaten by speed rushers to his inside, especially on stunts up front. If that’s his one shortcoming, though, I’m not looking to upset the applecart very much here. He’s more than earned his extension through his consistent availability, and the fact that he’s played at an above-average to good level throughout his career tells me that the Bills will definitely look to lock him in before he has the chance to test the free agent market. Whether it’s his last year with the Bills or the last year of his rookie contract before his new deal kicks in, Torrence should once again be a steady force up front for Buffalo.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 49 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - DECEMBER 11: Carolina Panthers guard Andrew Norwell (68) during the game between the Carolina Panthers and the San Diego Chargers on December 11, 2016 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, NC. Panthers win 28-16 over the Chargers. (Photo by Jim Dedmon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #49. Andrew Norwell Everyone loves a story about an undrafted free agent becoming a high level NFL player. Andrew Norwell is an interesting, and perhaps the least surprising version of that story. Norwell was a highly regarded recruit coming out of high school, ranked as either a four start or five star prospect, depending on where you look. He went to Ohio State, where he developed into a two time All Big Ten honoree. Despite the prestigious pedigree and decorated college career, Norwell somehow went undrafted in the 2014 NFL Draft. The Panthers were fortunate enough to scoop enough, and boy did that work out for them. He was forced into the starting lineup in Week 7 of his rookie year and would never relinquish that spot. He finished out the season as arguably the best rookie lineman and one of the best interior lineman in the whole league. He would go on to be a staple of the Panthers offensive line for the next three seasons and would perform as one of the league’s best guards, though he didn’t get a lot of recognition for it. He finally got his flowers after the 2017 season, when he was named first team all pro. The Jaguars would lure him away from Carolina with the largest contract for a guard in the entire NFL. Norwell would finish out his career with four seasons in Jacksonville and one last rodeo for Ron Rivera in Washington in 2022. Norwell was an interesting case of a highly regarded player throughout his amateur case that didn’t get drafted and then went on to become a very good NFL player. It’s like the least surprising success story for an undrafted free agent of all time. But credit to the Panthers for getting him to come here and giving him an opportunity to shine. Norwell only spent four seasons in Carolina, but he was one of the best players in the league at his position during those four years. His time coincided with what were some pretty good offensive seasons by the Rivera era Panthers standards, and he was a big part of that. He was part of the team that made it to Super Bowl 50 and the groups that went to the playoffs in 2014 and 2017. His rise from undrafted free agent and the elite player he was during a high point in Panthers history earns him spot number 49 on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time.

summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 16: Jaycee Horn #8 of the Carolina Panthers stands on the field during the NFL 2025 game between Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #50. Jaycee Horn The number 50 player on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time shouldn’t stay there for long. Jaycee Horn is still in his prime at 26 years old, but he’s already cemented himself as one of the best cornerbacks to come through Carolina. The Panthers made Horn the 8th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft after a standout college career and combine performance that ranked Horn as one of the most athletic cornerbacks ever tested. He immediately earned a starting spot, but his rookie season was derailed after just three games due to a broken foot. Horn returned for his sophomore season to play 13 games, intercepting three passes and allowing a passer rating of just 62.4. The injury bug bit again during the disastrous Frank Reich campaign of 2023. Horn had to leave the season opener with a hamstring injury, and he wouldn’t return until late November, well after the season was already lost. Still, he finished out the season healthy. He’s been able to maintain that health for each of the last two seasons, and his consistent presence on the field has helped boost his profile, resulting in Pro Bowl nods in both of those seasons. He’s reeled in six interceptions in those two years, five of them coming last season. And it seemed like all of last season’s interceptions were highlight reel plays. Jaycee Horn is now widely considered one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL. He gave up less than 500 receiving yards in each of the last two seasons and allows opposing quarterbacks to complete just over half their passes when they throw his way. He’s been a stellar corner even with little help in the way of quarterback pressure. The Panthers will hopefully have a better pass rush this season, even without Nic Scourton, which should only help Horn’s production even more. If that happens, he’ll surely climb this list. But for now, he’s penciled in at number 50 on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time.
