full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about today. NFL MVP: One non-QB candidate from each NFC team in 2026 | NFL.com Abdul Carter, OLB. As a rookie, Carter might have netted just four sacks, but he led Big Blue with 72 QB pressures — seventh-most in the league, per NGS — and a 15.4 percent QB pressure rate. The edge rusher showed improvement down the stretch, logging 3.5 of his four sacks in the final five weeks. With a strong get-off and more seasoning, Carter should put up bigger numbers in 2026. The Giants upgraded the surroundings for new defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, which should provide more opportunities for Carter to cause havoc on a consistent basis after ebbs and flows last season. Paul Schwartz on the OBJ/Harbaugh dynamic Will Odell Beckham Jr. make the team? @NYPost_Schwartz doesn't think so, but "wouldn't bet against him because [John] Harbaugh likes him." Blue Rush Training Camp Preview ➡️ https://t.co/5xOz4UQIhz pic.twitter.com/r7iN8gwfJa — New York Post Sports (@nypostsports) July 24, 2026 NFL training camp: 10 preseason breakout players | Yahoo Sports Giants DE Abdul Carter. Carter had an odd rookie season. He came in with a ton of hype as the third overall pick of last year’s draft, and had only four sacks. But the pressure stats were very good. He had the most quick pressures of any player in the NFL last season. The best guess is Carter turns a lot of those pressures into sacks this season. There’s no better way to get off to a good start than having a strong preseason, which would be a good sight for new Giants head coach John Harbaugh. Everyone would be excited to see Carter have a big preseason heading into his second NFL season. 20 Questions in 20 Days: Jaxson Dart in Year 2 | Giants.com Matt Citak: What the 23-year-old does as an encore from his promising rookie campaign will be an important factor in determining how much success the team has this season. With a new coaching staff in tow, Dart is now learning his second NFL offense in as many seasons. The young signal-caller picked up last year’s system rather quickly, and the hope is that he is able to do the same this year. Year 2 is always a big one for quarterbacks. Some players make the jump and take their game to the next level, which is what New England’s Drake Maye and Chicago’s Caleb Williams were able to do last year. Others suffer from the dreaded “sophomore slump” and see their game take a step back. Where Dart lands on this spectrum is the million-dollar question. Over-Under Win Predictions For Every NFL Team In 2026 | Bleacher Report New York Giants: Over 7.5. Bet Confidence Level: Moderate. I’m extremely high on the 2026 Giants. Jaxson Dart registered 24 combined passing/rushing touchdowns to five interceptions as a first-round rookie in 2025 and appears to be on track to take the reins as the franchise quarterback. He’ll now be coached by John Harbaugh and Matt Nagy, who bring considerable know-how and experience to this rising team. The offensive line should be better with top pick Francis Mauigoa on board, Dart now has vet Isaiah Likely as a safety valve, and he’s getting Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo back from injury. If that core can put it all together, a Giants team with several elite talents on defense should keep the momentum going after scoring 68 points in back-to-back wins to conclude 2025 with a run into or above the .500 range in 2026. NFL insider offers optimistic update on health of Giants owner John Mara | USAToday.com New York Giants co-owner and CEO John Mara received an encouraging health update from long-time NFL reporter Gary Myers. Mara publicly disclosed his cancer diagnosis in September 2025, stating he felt strong and optimistic while following a recommended treatment plan. He remained involved with the organization, even adjusting his chemotherapy schedule to participate fully in the coaching search that led to John Harbaugh’s hiring. “I can tell you that John looked great when I saw him three or four weeks ago. He really looked great. I hope that’s an indication that things are going well for him health-wise,” Myers said on the Bleav in Giants podcast. “The only other time I’ve seen him publicly was at Harbaugh’s press conference in January. And, to my eyes at least, he looked much better — to the point that if you didn’t know what he was battling, you wouldn’t know. That’s how good he looked.” From Big Blue View Revisiting the NY Giants’ 2023 draft class Which undrafted players will make the Giants’ 53-man roster? title: Three Jets will begin training camp on injury list
summary: Two members of the New York Jets will be on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, and one will be on the non-football injury (NFI) list as training camp begins per Zack Rosenblatt. As is the case each year, it’s important to know what these lists are and what they are not. Being on […]
full_text: Aug 16, 2025; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Jets defensive end Tyler Baron (94) following the game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rich Barnes-Imagn Images | Rich Barnes-Imagn Images Two members of the New York Jets will be on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, and one will be on the non-football injury (NFI) list as training camp begins per Zack Rosenblatt. DT T'Vondre Sweat is going on the NFI list to start training camp with a hamstring injury. It's not considered serious, per source. WR Tim Patrick and EDGE Tyler Baron will be placed on the PUP list at the start of camp as well. Patrick isn't expected to be out long, per… — Zack Rosenblatt (@ZackBlatt) July 25, 2026 As is the case each year, it’s important to know what these lists are and what they are not. Being on the PUP list simply means that a player is recovering from an injury that will keep him out of the first practice of training camp. It doesn’t necessarily mean the injury is serious. A player can come off the PUP list in training camp as soon as he is healthy enough to start practicing. It could even happen on day two. The player could suffer the exact same injury during the first practice, and he wouldn’t be on an injury list. The list tells us more about the timing of an injury than the recovery. The NFI list is the same. It is for players whose injury did not come participating in an NFL game or practice. So when you see these injuries described as “not serious” you should believe it.

title: Maybe NFL execs should look more at winning in evaluating Jalen Hurts
summary: It’s a week now since ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler put out his exhaustive annual work on how NFL executives, coaches and scouts view quarterbacks. It’s a provocative, thankless, comprehensive look at what decisionmakers feel. Somehow, someway, Jalen Hurts fell from No. 9 in 2025 to No. 17 in 2026. There is no question that Josh Allen, […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 04: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after scoring a four yard touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys during the first quarter in the game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 04, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s a week now since ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler put out his exhaustive annual work on how NFL executives, coaches and scouts view quarterbacks. It’s a provocative, thankless, comprehensive look at what decisionmakers feel. Somehow, someway, Jalen Hurts fell from No. 9 in 2025 to No. 17 in 2026. There is no question that Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, Joe Burrow, Matt Stafford and Lamar Jackson are among the best in the NFL. But are Dak Prescott, Justin Herbert, Drake Maye, Jared Goff and Caleb Williams really better than Hurts? Prescott, in terms of what he did last year (30 TDs vs. 10 INTs, 4,552 yards passing) has an argument. The others may not. Let’s simplify things. Let’s go with who of the previous 16 named above Hurts won more. Of the 16 ranked above Hurts, only Mahomes, Stafford and Sam Darnold have won Super Bowls. Hurts has a cumulative 22-13-1 record head-to-head against the previous 16 quarterbacks listed ahead of him. He is 5-3 in the postseason against those ahead of him and he’s a combined 8-2 against Stafford, Mahomes and Burrow. You would think that would count for something, right? Apparently, in the minds of some, winning does not. It seems as if winning in this discussion goes ignored. The Eagles were a one-dimensional team last season with an ailing offensive line, learning-as-he-went offensive coordinator and conservative approaches in the second half of games and still finished 11-6 and repeated as NFC East champions, the first team to do so in 21 years. Hurts had a little something to do with that. He has had his issues, holding on to the ball too long, not trusting himself to throw in tight windows, and not trusting the playcalling. Whether it is his choice to limit the times he runs on designed plays, or the coaching staff’s decision in trying to preserve him, it has not helped his overall development. We’re counting on an even year in the decade of the 2020s, and each time Hurts has been a starter in an even year of the 2020s, the Eagles have reached the Super Bowl (losing in 2022 and winning in 2024). Much of the Eagles’ 2026 success will rely on how well Hurts plays under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion—and how well he plays, if willing , under center. Hurts already has a pile of motivation to succeed this season. He will soon be up for another contract extension. The Eagles have not budged yet on that. It is a bottom line that refuses to go away: Hurts has no guaranteed salary in 2028. And there is no indication a contract extension is imminent. Hurts has a 57-25 career record in six years as the Eagles’ starting quarterback. Donovan McNabb was 92-49-1 in 11 years with one losing Super Bowl appearance. Randall Cunningham was 63-43-1 in 11 years with no Super Bowls. In the last four years Hurts has started, the Eagles have produced more victories than they ever have in any four-year span (50) in the history of the franchise—including two Super Bowls, winning one, over Reid’s 2000-2003 (46) or 2001-2004 (48) teams, or Ryan’s 1988-1991 (41) or 1989-1992 (42) teams. Winning must count for something. It’s all Hurts has done.

He’s ranked among the top 30 wide receivers in fantasy points per game in each of the last four seasons despite being the second option in the Eagles’ offense behind A.J. Brown. Smith has consistently graded between a 78.0 and 84.0 each season, putting him in the range of a great, but not elite, receiver. That’s culminated in an 89.4 career overall PFF grade, slotting 20th among wide receivers over the last five seasons. Because career grades reward sustained performance over larger samples, his sits above any single season’s mark. That is particularly impressive considering Smith’s career 20.5% target rate, tied for third-lowest among those 20 receivers. Smith has played more in the slot over the last two years than in his first three, but has improved most out wide. He posted an 89.9 PFF receiving grade out wide in 2025 with a 25.3% target rate. Smith also achieved 2.95 yards per route run when lined up out wide last season, tied for third-best behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Puka Nacua. Meanwhile, Smith’s grades in the slot have deteriorated over time. The Eagles traded away Brown and lost Jahan Dotson in free agency while adding Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown and Dontayvion Wicks. Lemon will primarily be a slot receiver, while both Brown and Wicks have played inside at times in their careers. We should see a significant shift toward Smith playing out wide rather than in the slot. The departure of Brown should help Smith’s target rate. 2026 Dynasty Riser, Faller and Longshot Predictions: Philadelphia Eagles – Dynasty League Football RISER: DeVonta Smith […] A.J. Brown has seen more targets, receptions and yards in every season for the Eagles since 2022 than Smith. While Smith is a fantastic receiver, Brown is more of the typical WR1 archetype as a bigger-bodied alpha. What’s notable is that in games without Brown, per Fantasy Points, Smith has been the WR8 in yards per route run, WR6 in targets per route run and WR4 in expected fantasy points per route run since 2022. With Brown leaving the team, Smith has a chance to leap into an alpha role – both for fantasy and on the field. LeBron James joins Michael Jordan in Philadelphia – BGN What was first just a dream has become a frightening reality for those who may oppose the City of Brotherly Love. Philadelphia now has both Michael Jordan AND LeBron James. Wow! Mike Gansey has orchestrated the greatest offseason in Philadelphia 76ers history – Liberty Ballers That transformation set the stage for the final stroke in Mike Gansey’s offseason masterpiece: the signing of LeBron James. The greatest NBA player of his generation is going to suit up for the Philadelphia 76ers. Now, I’m not going to suggest Gansey is personally responsible for James coming. More than anyone else in the league, LeBron has his own personal agency over how things will unfold in his career. The Klutch connection with Tyrese Maxey played a large part, I’m sure. But you can’t deny Gansey and LeBron being friendly from their Mr. Ohio Basketball days playing some sort of role. And everything else Gansey did with this roster allowed LeBron to view himself as a final missing piece in potentially bringing a championship to Philadelphia. If he was going to set aside personal history with his childhood home in Cleveland or somewhere where he spent a lot of years in Miami, it had to be for basketball reasons. This roster allowed Gansey and Bob Myers and whoever else to make the “basketball reasons” case to LeBron. The Sixers team that get swept by the Knicks in May isn’t snagging King James. LeBron James signs with Philadelphia 76ers on stunning 2-year deal – SB Nation LeBron James is trying to win the NBA’s GOAT argument on longevity, and he’s somehow still going strong on the brink of his 42nd birthday. James isn’t the best player in the NBA anymore, but he proved last season with the Los Angeles Lakers that he can still carry a team for long stretches and look like an All-NBA player in his best moments. James hit free agency for the fourth time in his career this summer, and now he has announced his next chapter after eight years in LA. James announced he’s signing with the Philadelphia 76ers for the 2026-27 season, in a move first reported by ESPN’s Shams Charania. This will be the 24th season of his career, and he’s spending it with a team no one could have seen coming a few weeks ago. Saquon Barkley, NFL players react to LeBron James joining Philadelphia: ‘Welcome to the city!’ – NFL.com LeBron James’ decision to join the Philadelphia 76ers shook up the sports world on Friday, inspiring reactions from the NBA legend’s fellow athletes, including in the NFL. Eagles teammates Saquon Barkley and Lane Johnson were especially excited to welcome James to the South Philadelphia Sports Complex. “Welcome to the city!” Barkley posted on X, tagging James. “Let me know when you tryna tee it up.” Barkley’s invitation comes two weeks after the star running back told reporters his pitch to bring James to the City of Brotherly Love. “I think it is one of the greatest sports towns in the world,” Barkley said at the time. “If you want to go out with a bang, I feel like a great spot would be in Philly, and bringing a championship to Philadelphia, you’d be remembered forever.” It appears James picked up what Barkley was putting down. Hurts – Good and Bad – Iggles Blitz One of his bad habits is bailing to the right and throwing the ball way out of bounds. That is fine on occasion, but Hurts does it too much. We know he can make plays outside the pocket. He’s got some big time highlight moments. There is a need for more consistency. This is an important season for Hurts. He’s won a Super Bowl for the Eagles, but Howie Roseman can’t entirely focus on the past. He’s got to think about the future and how Hurts fits in that. If Jalen can adapt to the new scheme and coaches, he could sign an extension in the future and stay QB for the foreseeable future. It will be interesting to see how this year plays out. title: Patriots’ Christian Gonzalez could make Joey Porter Jr. contract harder for Steelers
summary: The market for elite young cornerbacks may be about to take another significant leap, and that could have major implications for the Pittsburgh Steelers’ ongoing extension talks with Joey Porter Jr. According to New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, the organization has made Christian Gonzalez a contract offer that would make him the NFL’s highest-paid […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 25: Christian Gonzalez #0 of the New England Patriots lines up during the AFC Championship Playoff game between the New England Patriots and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The market for elite young cornerbacks may be about to take another significant leap, and that could have major implications for the Pittsburgh Steelers’ ongoing extension talks with Joey Porter Jr. According to New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, the organization has made Christian Gonzalez a contract offer that would make him the NFL’s highest-paid cornerback. “Coincidentally, it’s the highest contract in the Patriots franchise history,” Kraft said, via Mike Reiss . If Gonzalez ultimately signs a deal at that level, it would establish a new ceiling for the position just as the Steelers work toward what they hope will be a long-term agreement with Porter, one of the franchise’s foundational defensive players. The timing is notable because Gonzalez and Porter entered the league together as members of the 2023 NFL Draft class. While the Steelers have publicly expressed confidence that Porter is part of their long-term plans, any record-setting agreement for Gonzalez would likely strengthen the negotiating position of Porter’s representatives. The connection between the two extends beyond simply sharing the same draft class. Pittsburgh had an opportunity to draft Gonzalez with the 14th overall pick in 2023 but instead selected offensive tackle Broderick Jones after trading up three spots with the New England Patriots. The Patriots then remained on the board and landed Gonzalez with the 17th overall selection, a move that has proven to be one of the biggest steals of that draft. The Steelers later addressed their need at cornerback by selecting Porter with the 32nd overall pick. Since entering the NFL, both Gonzalez and Porter have emerged as two of the league’s brightest young defensive backs. Gonzalez has earned widespread recognition as one of football’s premier shutdown corners, while Porter has developed into Pittsburgh’s No. 1 cornerback, using his size, physicality, and press coverage ability to consistently match up against opposing top receivers. With both players eligible for second contracts, comparisons between the two have become inevitable. If Gonzalez resets the cornerback market, Porter’s camp will almost certainly point to that deal as the new standard for young, ascending players at the position. The Steelers have made retaining homegrown talent a priority in recent years, rewarding stars such as T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith, and Nick Herbig with lucrative extensions. Porter appears to be the next candidate, but the cost of doing business may continue to rise if Gonzalez’s record-setting contract becomes official. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: No Seahawks land on  nonfootball injury list for first time under Mike Macdonald
summary: The defending Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks have returned from their offseason break, with veterans having reported for training camp Friday. In the Mike Macdonald era, reporting to training camp has meant a laundry list of players landing on the nonfootball injury list to open training camp each year. In 2024 Anthony Bradford, Easton Gibbs, […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 20: Tory Horton #15 of the Seattle Seahawks carries the ball against the Houston Texans at Lumen Field on October 20, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The defending Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks have returned from their offseason break, with veterans having reported for training camp Friday. In the Mike Macdonald era, reporting to training camp has meant a laundry list of players landing on the nonfootball injury list to open training camp each year. In 2024 Anthony Bradford, Easton Gibbs, D.J. James, Nehemiah Pritchett and Dee Williams all landed on NFI at the start of Macdonald’s first training camp, while in 2025 it was Rylie Mills, Zy Alexanders, Tyrone Broden, Montorie Foster, D’Eryk Jackson and Isas Waxter. This training camp has been much different. Following rookies reporting earlier in July, the Seahawks placed rookie Deven Eastern on the PUP list , but no rookies landed on the NFI list. Then, once injured players reported, Nick Emmanwori, Kenny McIntosh and Tyrone Broden landed on the PUP list before Zach Charbonnet finished off the list of players landing on either the PUP or NFI lists . The difference between the PUP list and the NFI list is that players who find themselves on the PUP list suffered an injury either during a game the prior season or during offseason workouts. In contrast, those who wind up on the NFI list either suffered an injury in college were injured while training on their own away from the facility, or otherwise failed their physical from some reason other than an injury suffered in a game or practice. In the Macdonald era, the most common reason for a player to wind up on the NFI list is having failed their physical for being unable to complete the vaunted conditioning test Macdonald imported to the VMAC from his time with the Baltimore Ravens . So, with veterans having reported to training camp on Friday, Saturday was the moment of truth to see which, if any, veteran would be the first member of the roster to fail the conditioning test this year. Now, with the transaction wire for Saturday published by the league, the answer is no one. No one was placed on PUP by the Seahawks today, per NFL transaction wire. GREAT news! — Field Gulls (@FieldGulls) July 25, 2026 Not only did the Seahawks not add any players to the PUP list, there were no players moved to the NFI list, meaning every single member of the roster passed their physical, which means they all passed their conditioning test. That is a first in the Macdonald era, and shows that players didn’t spend the offseason being lazy and getting fat in spite of having thumped the New England Patriots 29-13 in Super Bowl LX to lay claim to bragging rights as world champions until at least Valentine’s Day next year.

title: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan recovering from ‘severe concussion’ after car accident
summary: The Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers have a fierce rivalry, which 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan reignited after some very down seasons post-Jim Harbaugh. With training camp set to begin for both teams this weekend, it’s been revealed that Coach Shanahan is on the mend following a car accident in which he suffered several […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 07: Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers shakes hands with Head coach Mike Macdonald of the Seattle Seahawks after the game at Lumen Field on September 07, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers have a fierce rivalry, which 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan reignited after some very down seasons post-Jim Harbaugh. With training camp set to begin for both teams this weekend, it’s been revealed that Coach Shanahan is on the mend following a car accident in which he suffered several significant injuries. ESPN has the details of the July 14 accident: Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs and his hand, needed more than 40 stitches in his face, and suffered a severe concussion during a July 14 car crash when he collided with an SUV near his northern California home, according to sources familiar with the situation. He was taken by paramedics to a local hospital, where he spent much of that day before being released. The other driver was not injured, according to Palo Alto Lt. Nicholas Martinez. While Shanahan will be at camp in a limited capacity, assistant head coach Chris Foerster and team coordinators will effectively fill the head coach responsibilities for the foreseeable future. A news conference will be held by 49ers general manager John Lynch later today (Saturday, Jul. 25). According to the police report, no one was cited, both Shanahan and the other driver were cooperative with authorities, and drugs and alcohol were not involved in the accident. Rivalries aside, it’s good to know that his injuries are non-life threatening. It’s still nevertheless a scary and unfortunate ordeal to go through, and hopefully Coach Shanahan makes a full recovery. Given the Seahawks have ties to Shanahan through offensive line coach John Benton, new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury, run game coordinator Justin Outten, and quarterback Sam Darnold, I’m sure they’ll be sending their well wishes to him if they haven’t already.

title: The Seahawks are running it forward with focus, camaraderie, and hunger
summary: Over the cusp of training camp, it is perhaps the perfect time to turn the final page on the Seattle Seahawks’ 2025 Super Bowl-winning team. The final three episodes of Making a Champion (which started with John Schneider) centered around Rashid Shaheed (ep. 7), Sam Darnold (ep. 8) and Mike Macdonald (ep. 9). Those tied […]
full_text: Over the cusp of training camp, it is perhaps the perfect time to turn the final page on the Seattle Seahawks’ 2025 Super Bowl-winning team. The final three episodes of Making a Champion ( which started with John Schneider ) centered around Rashid Shaheed ( ep. 7 ), Sam Darnold ( ep. 8 ) and Mike Macdonald ( ep. 9 ). Those tied the series—and really the whole vibe of that title squad together in a neat bow before the slate is wiped clean for another campaign. The Focus One of the things themes that stood out when hearing from all three men, was how focused, disciplined and committed to the mission, this team felt. Shaheed was asked when he realized that the NFC West has a different level of intensity in their level of competition. He said, “It didn’t take me long at all. It took me two drives to realize how serious this team was and how on track we were to our goals.” Shaheed referenced “the intensity and the urgency that everybody had in the building, from the coaches to the players: everyone just believed in one another.” Shaheed went on to discuss organizational mindset, even while up big (like against the San Francisco 49ers): “I feel like, with this team, it’s definitely foot on the gas. I feel like that’s what our coaches instilled in us: win, loss, up on the board, tie game, you kind of just stay even keeled throughout it all. And you know, just keep your head down, keep grinding it out, ‘cus in this game, you never know. This game could flip like that, as we’ve seen. so, just keep the foot on the gas and you know, never let up. That’s the mindset we’ve had, and that’s how we’re able to finish games so strong.” Sam Darnold added to the chorus of individuals in this outfit that are constantly able to block out the noise: “You can’t give into, like, anything that they’re saying; whether it’s good or bad, ‘cus like, you’re investing in it. If you invest in something that someone on TV says that’s good about you, subconsciously, you’re going to hold their opinion to a different weight. If they say something bad about you, you can be like, ‘oh, I don’t care’, but you really do, because you validated it by saying, ‘they told me I was good, that’s awesome for me.’” He goes on to say, “For me, it was just like, not paying attention to what anyone said. That really changed things for me, and I started doing that a few years ago. I really do think football is like, the ultimate team sport. when you start caring what people say about you, that kind of goes against everything that I grew up loving about football. It is the ultimate team sport, and I know that it takes a team to have success. It’s just up to me to be smart with the football and put the ball in the end zone.” The Bond Another common thread across these interviews was something we’ve heard before. The special level of bonding that took place on this team, in particular. All three guys have come from different team backgrounds and expressed that this was different. Shaheed spoke on the media criticism and doubt of QB, Sam Darnold throughout the season and up until the Super Bowl game: “I feel like the noise and all that other stuff, it didn’t really phase him, or us. We know what type of player Sam was, we knew what type of leader he was. He’s proven that he can win games. You know, the media is going to say what they want to say, but as long as Sam goes out there and continues to lead and win games here; and to see what he did in his first year in the organization, not a lot of guys can do that and handle it the way he did and ultimately win a championship.” It’s clear that the members of the Seattle Seahawks care about each other’s success. That was reinforced by the man in charge on gameday. Macdonald on seeing the vets win a championship who had been waiting for a long time in their careers to get to this point: “I’m not thinking that they were thinking, ‘wow, finally, it’s my time.’ It’s like, their mentality was just like… they were excited for our team. I think that’s how we were able to become the team we became, because we didn’t have all these guys that were kind of just, ‘hey, I’ve been in a league for X-amount of years. I’ve never been to the Super Bowl.’ I’m sure they were thinking that, but their actions didn’t really back that up, you know.’ The Hunger What we all want to know, is if the 2026 Seattle Seahawks have what it takes to go back to the top of the mountain? Mike Macdonald on the Super Bowl experience: “One thing I didn’t anticipate was how many media members are out there, like across the world, had really no idea about who we were and what we did, and like, our guys. It just felt like we were this team that showed up that they had no idea, you know, how we did things. And so, for that to come through for the world to show, or kind of learned who the Seahawks were was a really great byproduct of the whole week.” Coach Mike has now experienced the high-level East-Coast bias that all Seattle athletes from time immemorial have had to embrace. The underdog mentality. I like to hear that edge in Macdonald’s bullish belief in this team. Episode 8 of Making A Champion. Out now. Watch here » https://t.co/hqHNERJWXZ pic.twitter.com/EqNOH07gxv — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) July 14, 2026 Of course, the thesis of these sit-downs was to ask each participant to define what made the 2025 team a championship outfit. Shaheed on what made the 2025 Seahawks a championship team: “I feel like everybody, um… we grind. We work here. Coming from New Orleans to here, I saw the difference in what a championship football team really—no disrespect to New Orleans—but you know, obviously you just kind of feel what needs to be done. Now that we’ve done that, I feel like we can kind of, carry it on to the team that is the 2026 Seahawks. Super excited about that.” That’s great focus. Darnold on what made the 2025 Seahawks a championship team: “I would say how close we were. I would say, just the chemistry that we all—the bond, the love that he had for each other.” That’s great unity. Macdonald on what made the 2025 Seahawks a championship team: “I think them adopting the M.O.B. ties mentality, of just how we’re going to do it every day. So, what’s included in that? It’s the daily mentality about who we want to be. It’s a focusing. It’s about us. It’s the connection with the team. That’s what made it special. So, X’s and O’s are important, but not that important. That is all of it. The mindset, the team building and the constant chasing of edges that Coach Macdonald often speaks of. From all indications, the 2026 Seattle Seahawks seem to understand that last year is last year. They also seem to embrace that there is more room for growth on a team that has laid the foundation for continued success. It all starts in training camp.

title: 49ers HC  Kyle Shanahan involved in a car accident; John Lynch provides updates
summary: The San Francisco 49ers issued a statement on Saturday after head coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs, and his hand, and needed over 40 stitches in his face. Shanahan also suffered a severe concussion after colliding with an SUV near his […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 14: Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers looks on from the sidelines against the Tennessee Titans in the first quarter at Levi's Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers issued a statement on Saturday after head coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs, and his hand, and needed over 40 stitches in his face. Shanahan also suffered a severe concussion after colliding with an SUV near his northern California home, according to Schefter. According to the statement issued by the team, Shanahan’s injuries were non-life-threatening: “San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week where he suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers. Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care. Assistant Head Coach Chris Foerster along with team coordinators will handle head coach responsibilities during this period.” Schefter tweeted that Shanahan informed the coaching staff of the accident on Tuesday, while the players are slowly getting the news after the car accident was confirmed today. Schefter added that paramedics took Shanahan to the local hospital, where he spent much of the day before being released. The other driver was not injured, according to Palo Alto Lieutenant Nicholas Martinez. There were no drugs or alcohol involved, per Martinez. Neither driver was cited for the collision, while both were cooperative with the police. Kyle’s update, 11:38 a.m. PT: John Lynch said Shanahan had “lingering effects” from the car accident. The team is going to essentially place Shanahan in the concussion protocol and let the team doctors determine when Shanahan will fully return. Lynch said that Shanahan is still in the building. When asked if Shanahan wouldn’t make the trip to Australia for Week 1, Lynch said, “That’s not something we’re anticipating. That’s not what I’ve heard from the doctors. Just like I said with the doctors, the timeline kind of takes care of itself. He’s got to meet certain markers. I think the expectation is that long before that, he’ll be better. But again, everybody responds to these things differently. We’re going to do whatever it takes to have him right when he comes back. That’s the right thing to do.” Lynch added that we’ll likely see Shanahan on the field early in training camp, but he won’t speak to the team or the media until he’s fully cleared in the recovery from his concussion.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers place 4 players on the active/PUP List; sign former 6th-round tight end

Taking his roster spot will be tight end Tanner McLachlan, a 6th-rounder from the 2024 NFL Draft out of Arizona. McLachlan is a big body at 6’5 1/8″, […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch announced a series of moves Saturday morning. The Niners waived undrafted rookie tight end Khalil Dinkins with a non-football injury. Taking his roster spot will be tight end Tanner McLachlan, a 6th-rounder from the 2024 NFL Draft out of Arizona. McLachlan is a big body at 6’5 1/8″, with surprising speed. He ran a 4.61 40-yard dash, which is in the 87th percentile. His 10-yard split of 1.58 was in the 84th percentile. McLachlan was most recently with the Bengals. Defensive tackle Evan Anderson will be released at some point on Saturday. Lynch said there will be a corresponding move, although that hasn’t been announced yet. The following players will begin training camp on the active/PUP list: TE George Kittle (Achilles) RB Isaac Guerendo (pec) DL Mykel Williams (ACL) DT Alfred Collins (shoulder) Lynch said, “George’s rehab is coming tremendous. I know you guys have heard from him. He’s doing really well. That’s very exciting. He’s doing everything possible to be ready for Week 1. We’re thrilled with his process.” For Williams, Lynch said, “What I would say with Mykel, he’s making every effort to be ready for Week 1. We’ll see if that’s a reality. We’ll let the markers and the medical staff kind of dictate that out.” As for Collins, the 49ers are expecting him back in “the second window. Don’t hold us to that, but that’s the plan right now. If he keeps hitting the markers, that’s about when Alfred will be back.” Players placed on the PUP list before training camp count as part of the 90-man roster. However, they cannot practice until they’re physically cleared and removed from PUP. Since the four players are on the active/PUP List, they can be removed from the list at any point during training camp.

title: George Kittle on the Brandon Aiyuk Situation: ‘I feel [the 49ers] have tried’
summary: Don’t be expecting Brandon Aiyuk’s teammates to be jumping to his defense anytime soon. Well, at least his fellow tight end. George Kittle has arrived at the San Francisco 49ers’ facility for training camp and hasn’t heard much, nor is he saying much. The tight end spoke with Chris Simms about the still-going Brandon Aiyuk […]
full_text: Jan 11, 2026; Philadelphia, PA, USA; San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle (85) looks on during warmups prior to an NFC Wild Card Round game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Don’t be expecting Brandon Aiyuk’s teammates to be jumping to his defense anytime soon. Well, at least his fellow tight end. George Kittle has arrived at the San Francisco 49ers’ facility for training camp and hasn’t heard much, nor is he saying much. The tight end spoke with Chris Simms about the still-going Brandon Aiyuk situation and didn’t offer much on the defense of the soon-to-be-former 49ers wide receiver. Kittle used his own experiences with contract negotiations in his response, which winds up making the whole Aiyuk situation even more petty: A majority of this has come during the summer break. I literally got back to the building yesterday, and I have not seen anyone or heard anyone talk about it. I would say, in general, I feel like I know basically everything that’s happened and what’s gone on and I can’t share all of that cause it’s not my business to share or tell, but I just want to let you know that I feel like the Niners have done a very good job throughout the entire process and have tried. Kyle has tried, John has tried, teammates have tried, and this is where we are. I think the organization itself has done a really good job. Like I said, I know plenty of things and I don’t ever want to single out a player. I don’t want ever want to point a finger at anybody, but I’ve been here for 10 years and I’ve been treated with nothing but respect and love my entire career. I feel like I’ve done it the right way as long as I can. Contract negotiations are always hard for everybody. You just your best to sit out and not be sensitive about it. I will say Richard Sherman gave me advice during my first contract negotiation: Contracts are like braces. They hurt and they suck the entire time. And once you get your braces off and you get paid, you don’t ever remember having them. That’s the mindset you have to have. You get offended by something and you hold onto it, that’s kinda on you, because everyone goes through contract negotiations and they are all difficult. While Kittle can’t pull back the curtain and get granular on who did what in this debacle, he makes a good point about contracts. The 49ers’ issue (in a nutshell) was that Aiyuk’s rehab was not being done at the facility and the ghosting that followed. While Aiyuk’s current issue is the guaranteed money getting pulled, not being traded (and a bajillion other things), all of this could have started with a growing resentment for how his contract negotiations went in 2024. Kittle is no stranger to contract negotiations, and it’s a safe assumption the 49ers were playing the negotiating game with him as well. The difference, as Kittle said, is that once the negotiations are over, things are forgotten, the parties align, and everyone goes back to work. Unless, of course, you are Brandon Aiyuk. Taking this, Aiyuk may have signed the contract but didn’t wash the stain of all the negotiations off. Given how drawn out the Aiyuk contract went (like right up to the final seconds), he signed the deal with one foot in the door and one out. That much is obvious, but for how much money he was guaranteed, he really did sacrifice a lot for a petty grudge.

Onto today’s links… Agent’s Take: Brandon Aiyuk has only himself to blame for 49ers limbo chaos Aiyuk claimed he fired Williams in November. Williams was still listed as Aiyuk’s agent of record by the NFLPA until the end of June, when Aiyuk sent a written notice as required by their agent regulations. Presumably, Aiyuk told Williams verbally last November that his services were no longer needed. Although Williams hadn’t received a termination letter, it’s understandable that he wouldn’t be trying to protect Aiyuk’s interest anymore after such a conversation. There wasn’t anything preventing Williams from making the split official at any time by sending Aiyuk a termination letter. For example, Antonio Brown and Johnny Manziel were fired by their respective agents. I don’t doubt that Aiyuk was told by the NFLPA and/or Williams that he would be released in early June at the latest. That was likely before Aiyuk went AWOL. The 49ers are less inclined to reward what can reasonably be viewed as negative behavior. George Kittle reveals one area where Kyle Shanahan has grown as 49ers coach “His situational awareness, in my opinion, has grown so much,” Kittle said. “He’s been the head coach for going on 10 years now, and he’s just learned constantly — this part of the game matters the most. Got to hang onto the ball before halftime. Don’t let the other team score. Turnovers, whatever it is. Our whole team has realized that, too. We’ve all grown with it.” “Sometimes we get one of the most difficult game plans I’ve ever seen in my entire life, and then another game, it’ll be the easiest game plan I’ve ever seen, but it’s versus a better team,” Kittle said. “I’m just like, ‘Kyle, what are we doing?’ But then they all work, and I’m just like, oh well. I’m having a great time regardless.” Former All-Pro WR predicts career year for 49ers wideout Coming to San Francisco, the 32-year-old is expected to be the team’s top wide receiver for Brock Purdy to target, and some, including legendary NFL wide receiver Chad Johnson, believe that Evans will be great for the 49ers. In a post on social media, Johnson predicted that Evans will catch 98 passes for 1,343 yards and 12 touchdowns in 2026. That would be the most receptions, the second-most receiving yards and tied for the fourth-most touchdowns that he’s had in year. With Evans coming off of a rough season where he missed nine games due to injury, those are lofty predictions for this year, but if the 49ers got even 80% of that production, they’d probably be thrilled this year. 25 predictions for 49ers’ season: How many games will they win? Should you save up for playoff tickets? (Paywall) 10. Sack leaders: Nick Bosa (10), Osa Odighizuwa (4.5), Mykel Williams (4), Romello Height (4). 11. Kittle will make his season debut in Week 2 after suffering a torn Achilles in January. 12. Purdy will miss two starts with a sprained AC joint. His season stats: 3,772 yards, 25 TDs, 11 INTs, completing 68.1% of his passes. 13. Their first draft pick, WR De’Zhaun Stribling, will have 36 catches for 458 yards and 3 TDs. 14. A running back who is not on the current roster will have at least 40 carries. 15. A pass rusher who is not on the current roster will have at least four sacks. Every Player on the Roster Bubble for the 49ers: Who’s In, Who’s Out Running Back Isaac Guerendo Guerendo will need to make it with special teams. Wide Receiver Demarcus Robinson Robinson could prove more reliable than Kirk in the preseason. Wide Receiver Junior Bergen Bergen could earn a spot by returning kicks and punts. Tight End Brayden Willis The tight end room is thin, opening a door for Willis. Offensive Tackle Austen Pleasants Pleasants could outshine one of Vederian Lowe or Enrique Cruz. Offensive Lineman Nick Zakelj The versatility of Zakelj gives him a chance to stick around. Interior Defensive Lineman Evan Anderson The following three linemen will all compete for a fifth spot. They will also compete with Gracen Halton for the fourth spot. 49ers starter entering ‘make-or-break’ season, per PFF PFF’s Bradley Locker wrote that Lenoir is one of 10 players on Super Bowl contenders who make or break his respective teams’ 2026 campaign. Locker pointed to a step back in coverage and run defense as reasons for concern with Lenoir. It’s still remarkable that the 49ers reached the divisional round given their defense finished 31st in success rate. While injuries and issues affected almost every level of the unit, Lenoir was also more ineffective than usual. Lenoir led San Francisco in defensive snaps but posted a 65.7 PFF coverage grade, good for the 62nd percentile — a dip from the 74-plus coverage grades he posted in each of the previous two seasons. His 99.8 passer rating allowed still ranked 20th-highest among qualified corners, and he graded in the 51st percentile in coverage at outside corner. He was also flagged a career-high 10 times, and his run-defense grade fell to a personal low of 44.3.

full_text: Editor’s note: We’ll be running down some key roster battles in the the leadup to Washington Commanders training camp later this month. John Portis has taken the lead on this series that will look at rookies, veterans, and free agents who are fighting for playing time in July , but Christian Paolantonio hops in for this look at young receivers vying for increased roles . The wide receiver position has been a consistent discussion point surrounding the Washington Commanders heading into the 2026 season. Whether it’s Brandon Aiyuk or Stefon Diggs, media and fans alike continue to debate whether the team should add another threat for Jayden Daniels and the offense. No matter which direction the team decides to go, the previously added depth poses a threat to recent draft picks like Luke McCaffrey and Jaylin Lane , who have impressed on special teams alongside slight offensive success. The current Commanders wideouts group heading into training camp also includes Terry McLaurin, Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown, Treylon Burks, Van Jefferson, Jacoby Jones, Nick Nash, Jaden Bradley, and Chris Hilton Jr. Outside McLaurin, Williams, Brown, and Burks, it begins to become murky as to who will be on the roster for Week 1. Van Jefferson reportedly impressed during OTAs and minicamp, but training camp and the preseason will be the true test for most of these fringe guys. While both McCaffrey and Lane should make the team unless one falls completely flat, playing time could be impacted by how this battle goes. When comparing McCaffrey and Lane, their on-field production is similar thus far in their young careers. In McCaffrey’s first two seasons, he played in 26 games with 29 receptions on 39 targets, totaling 371 receiving yards and three touchdowns. McCaffrey’s 2025 season was unfortunately cut short after he suffered a broken collarbone against Seattle in Week 9. McCaffrey’s special teams impact was also felt in 2025 on kickoffs, as he finished with the third-highest kickoff ( 29.6 yards ) return average in the NFL. Lane’s rookie campaign included 16 catches on 32 targets, finishing with 225 receiving yards in 15 games played. Lane’s impact was certainly felt more so on the punt-return team, as he finished 5th in the NFL in yards per return (13.7) along with two return touchdowns (tied for league-lead). The underlying question remains: Does Washington have the roster space for two receivers who are also special teams returners? With Lane entering his second season and a full NFL offseason under his belt, we should expect a more comfortable and savvy version of the former Hokie this upcoming year on offense. McCaffrey will enter training camp with heavier expectations than previous years due to the sheer openness of the wide receivers position on Washington’s current roster. The entire landscape of the offense could change with the addition of Diggs or Aiyuk or another veteran, but McCaffrey and Lane now have an opportunity to earn legitimate snaps for new coordinator David Blough’s unit. Both young wideouts are entering a critical summer, especially with an entirely new offense to grasp. That’s paired with new competition across the board with vets like Brown, Jefferson and UDFAs like Jaden Bradley and Chris Hilton Jr. carrying a chip on their shoulder. Keep an eye and ear out for camp reports/updates involving McCaffrey and Lane as preseason rolls along and Week 1 at Philadelphia approaches. Jayden connects on a deep ball to Luke McCaffrey! title: Commanders CB Trey Amos, two others placed on PUP before training camp
summary: The Commanders made some roster designation changes on Saturday morning, a day before the full squad reports to training camp. full_text: The Commanders made some roster designation changes on Saturday morning, a day before the full squad reports to training camp. Secomd-year CB Trey Amos was placed on the active/physically unable to perform list, suggesting the fractured fibula that ended his rookie season early will prevent him from starting camp on time. That’s not massive cause for concern, as Amos has claimed that he’s on the right track towards recovery. Defensive linemen Deatrich Wise Jr. and Dorance Armstrong were also placed on active/PUP. Armstrong has been rehabbing a knee injury while Wise is recovering from a torn quadriceps . Undrafted rookie cornerback Fred Davis II was placed on the active/non-football illness list. As a note, being placed on the “active” versions of these lists means the players still count against the Commanders’ 90-man roster limit. While they will use a roster exemption on T.J. Maguranyanga as part of the International Player Pathway program, the Commanders remain one player over the limit at this time. If any of the three players on PUP aren’t cleared by roster cuts downs, they will have to miss the first four games of the season. They can be activated from the PUP list at any time during training camp to rejoin the team in practice. One name that’s not on the list is DT Tim Settle who was placed on injured reserve by the Texans last season due to a foot injury. He had surgery after the Week 13 injury, and rejoined the team that drafted him earlier this year. Settle had been part of the sideline crew that was rehabbing injuries, but will be good to go for the start of training camp.

But I do like the competition in the group. Like I said, I thought Rachaad’s brought some things on the, you know, the catching and receiving phase of things. To see Bill [RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt], to see the guys get back into the mix, to see the two young running backs, what they can add. I don’t know yet, but I think we’ll for sure be more than just one.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Can any edge rusher stay consistent through the season? Oweh has had one season of double-digit sacks in his career, and he was a no-show until he was traded to Los Angeles midseason. Chaisson was considered a bust with the Jacksonville Jaguars and Las Vegas Raiders, and Armstrong had his best season last year, but he is coming off a serious injury, and he should not be counted on to carry the load fully. Oweh is being brought on to be the team’s top pass rusher, and his cap number backs up that. One potential scenario to look out for is inside linebacker Frankie Luvu coming in on passing situations and playing on the edge. All in all, the Commanders have the depth and talent to have a very productive group, but they do not have a proven, consistent “war daddy” in the room heading into camp. New defensive coordinator Daronte Jones will have better pieces to work with than his predecessor Joe Whitt, but it is up to him to scheme his chess pieces on the board. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Heavy.com Sonny Styles Preparing for Hybrid Workload Speaking on 106.7 The Fan , Mitchell asked, “You know that big nickel thing they used to play? What if you have four and your big nickel is actually Sunny? Yeah. Sunny now is your fourth linebacker playing right on the nose of that damn tight end.” [R]easons to believe Styles will operate as a so-called “Big Nickel” [are] based on the former Ohio State star’s own experience, what Jones will do with this defense, and how often the Commanders have used the niche position, both under current head coach Dan Quinn and his predecessor Ron Rivera. [I]t’s not a stretch to envisage Styles spending [time] at safety in the pros. The case has only been strengthened by Styles “working with Defensive Back Specialist-Coach Aye in San Diego” this offseason, per highlights posted by Substack writer Hykeem Walker , who noted Styles exhibited “Elite footwork” and “DB Hands.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Commanders rookie Joshua Josephs could have a path to early playing time The explosiveness and burst off the snap were as advertised. What was most surprising was Josephs’ ability to drop back into coverage and make plays. That’s something most pure pass-rushers cannot do effectively enough, so it could bring a different dynamic to Daronte Jones’ defense if the same trend continues. It’s a good start from Josephs. The real tests are coming. Things will obviously get a lot more intense over training camp, especially when the pads go on. Joint practices and the preseason will be a strong measuring stick for the first-year pro, which could potentially determine what his role will be in 2026. If he shines, Josephs could form a core part of the defensive edge rotation . Odafe Oweh, K’Lavon Chaisson, and the returning Dorance Armstrong Jr. will lead the charge, but it would be surprising if the Tennessee product wasn’t next in line. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Predicting who survives the Commanders’ six fiercest training camp battles Commanders WR2 and WR3 Much has been made about the Washington Commanders’ wide receiver options. Some believe more is needed, with the team being linked to almost every big-name free agent or potential trade target. General manager Adam Peters hasn’t moved as yet, which indicates a willingness to let the young options behind Terry McLaurin fight it out this summer. McLaurin is the alpha; that’s not up for discussion. Several others will be fighting for the WR2 and WR3 roles, and they will all fancy their chances of securing their share of targets within David Blough’s system. Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown are reclamation projects. Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane, undrafted free agent Jaden Bradley, and third-round rookie Antonio Williams are unproven. Van Jefferson Jr. at least has some previous production, but things have tailed off for the veteran pass-catcher in recent years. The Commanders will be watching developments closely. If Peters isn’t satisfied, acquiring another dependable wideout instantly becomes his top priority. But it’s also worth remembering how much tight end Chig Okonkwo and running back Rachaad White are expected to feature in the passing attack. This is hard to call. One could make a strong case for almost everybody. But looking at the scheme Blough plans to operate, Burks may end up on the outside with Williams in the slot to start the season. title: Commanders EDGE Odafe Oweh poised for career-best season in Washington
summary: In this week’s Reacts survey, we asked Hogs Haven readers to rate their confidence that this year’s big offseaon free agent signing, edge rusher Odafe Oweh, will live up to his 4-year, $96-million contract in 2026. The results are unsurprising, with more than half of all respondents saying that they are ‘generally confident’, which would […]
full_text: In this week’s Reacts survey , we asked Hogs Haven readers to rate their confidence that this year’s big offseaon free agent signing, edge rusher Odafe Oweh, will live up to his 4-year, $96-million contract in 2026. The results are unsurprising, with more than half of all respondents saying that they are ‘generally confident’, which would equate to a grade of 4 on a 5-point scale. Visit our partners at FanDuel In fact, 70% of respondents said that they are either generally confident or absolutely confident — a strong indication of support for a player who peaked with 10 sacks in 2024, but who went sack-less in his first 5 games of the 2025 season before being traded from the Ravens to the Chargers. That change of scenery seemed to do Oweh a lot of good. He tallied 7.5 sacks in 12 games in his powder-blue jersey — that pace put him on track for 10.5 sacks in 17 games. What are the expectations, then, for a player who is being paid $24m per season as a pass rusher? According to Over the Cap , there are four NFL edge rushers currently on contracts with an average annual cap hit of between $22 million and $24.5 million: George Karlaftis, Andrew Van Ginkel, Odafe Oweh, and Montez Sweat. Here’s a snapshot of some key metrics for those 4 players for the past two seasons combined: Combined 2024 & 2025 statistics Source : Pro Football Reference George Karlaftis leads in 3 metrics: total defensive snaps played, total pressures, and snaps per pressure. Andrew Van Ginkel tallied the most sacks of the four players listed. Odafe Oweh stacks up pretty well overall despite playing the fewest snaps of the group. He is second in sacks and highly efficient, ranking #1 in snaps per sack and #2 in snaps per pressure. It looks like this salary range should buy an NFL team around 674 defensive snaps, with 26 pressures and 7.5 sacks in a 17-game season. In 2024 & 2025, Oweh produced just about that number of pressures and at least that many sacks while playing significantly fewer snaps. If he only reproduces what he did in 2025, this analysis indicates that he’ll be earning his AAV of $24 million per season. But can Commanders fans expect even more from Oweh now that he has signed with Washington? A Transition from Rotational to Alpha Role Historically, Oweh’s raw numbers were capped because he was utilized as a rotational asset rather than a true foundational piece. In 2025, he played the first five weeks struggling for snaps in Baltimore before a midseason trade to the Los Angeles Chargers. Once integrated into Jesse Minter’s defense in Los Angeles, Oweh’s efficiency skyrocketed, culminating in a dominant 17.3% quarterback pressure percentage and a franchise playoff-record 3-sack, 2-forced fumble performance against New England. The turning point for his career has now arrived in 2026. Recognizing this elite trajectory, the Commanders signed Oweh to a massive four-year, $96 million contract ($68 million guaranteed) to serve as the undisputed “alpha” edge rusher. By stepping out from the shadow of playing behind other veteran rushers, Oweh is expected to see his snap share rise from 575 snaps per year to 670+ defensive snaps in Washington’s scheme. If he can maintain his per-snap efficiency with the increased snap count, he could generate roughly 28 pressures and 10.5 sacks in 2026. If he plays closer to 800 snaps this season, then his production could align closely with that of Andrew Van Ginkel, who averaged 796 defensive snaps per season over the past two years. Backed by a defensive scheme explicitly designed to isolate his 90th-percentile athletic traits and a contract that guarantees he will be on the field as much as possible, Oweh possesses both the proven efficiency and the volume opportunity to make 2026 the most productive year of his career.
